quoted_text:
I met the man once.

After having lunch with Michael Piller at Paramount, he walked me over to tour the sets for “Deep Space Nine” and “Star Trek: The Next Generation,” the latter of which was in production.

I overheard an AD say Patrick Stewart had wrapped earlier, so I was surprised to see him still there.

Michael explained that Stewart made it a point to read off-camera lines for his fellow cast members, including, in this particular case, a guest star.

We were introduced, and I found Stewart’s demeanor to be a mix of commanding and casual. After complimenting him on his performances as Sejanus in “I, Claudius” and Lenin in “Fall of Eagles,” his posture noticeably changed.

In fact, the director of the episode began ribbing him about how he was now “standing up straighter,” as Stewart wryly remarked in that sonorous voice: “There are a few of your kind that know my work from before.”

When I tried to compliment him for hanging around for another performer’s coverage, he told me the story how, on his very first film, Rod Steiger insisted on doing the same for him, overriding a harried director who wanted the script supervisor to dispassionately read the dialogue so the scene could be banged out more quickly.

We chatted for a few minutes about Shakespeare and mutual acquaintances before he returned to the scene underway.

All the cast members from “Star Trek: The Next Generation” I’ve interacted with have been delightful and gracious. It seemed to be a harmonious ensemble in which they had cast not only the right actors for each role, but the right people.

It started with the captain. 🎭

text:
What just happened in Poland is something every Western citizen should look at squarely. Because it's the trailer for what's coming to the rest of us.

Friday night in Warsaw, the president of the Constitutional Tribunal and his vice-president were "suspended" for a month. The announcement appeared on the Tribunal's own website, which the Tribunal's leadership says was unlawfully taken over. Right after, riot police deployed around the country's highest court and entered the building. The President of the Republic, Karol Nawrocki, was mid-flight to Senegal. He turned the plane around.

Read that again, slowly. In a European Union member state, in 2026, police walk into the constitutional court and the head of state has to rush home.

This is not an accident. It's the endpoint of a method. December 2023: barely in office, the Tusk government cuts the signal of the public news channel and puts public television into liquidation. Then it stops publishing the Constitutional Tribunal's rulings in the official gazette. When the Tribunal suspends one of its reforms, a ministry calmly replies that the court has "no legal basis" to operate. The justice minister moves to strip the court president's immunity. And when none of that is enough, they send in the uniforms.

The official story is "we are restoring the rule of law." It's always the official story. Nobody has ever dismantled a democracy while announcing they were dismantling a democracy.

Now zoom out. Why now?

Because the globalist project is losing its grip. They lost the media war: people get their information elsewhere, compare, verify, and no longer trust the official line. They lost the trust of the people. And the countries that are bouncing back, the ones finding their energy, their birth rates, their pride again, are precisely the ones that understood that the Brussels machine, as it runs today, is not the cure but the disease. Poles elected Nawrocki against the system's candidate. The message was clear.

When a system loses trust, it has two options: reform or harden. They chose. All-in.

Think of an organ transplant. The body rejects the organ. The surgeon doesn't conclude the organ is incompatible. He raises the immunosuppressants. Then raises them again. Until the body can no longer defend itself at all. That's the mechanism now in motion: platform regulation in the name of fighting "disinformation," Chat Control that keeps coming back to the table, the digital euro, a presidential election annulled in Romania in 2024, and now police inside a constitutional court.

And this is where history should chill us. No totalitarian regime of the 20th century began with people who thought they were evil. They all began with elites convinced they were right against their own people, and ready to suspend the rules "temporarily" to save the people from themselves. We know how that ended. Millions dead. I'm not saying it's tomorrow. I'm saying it's the slope, and you don't climb back up a slope once you've started sliding.

And don't think this stops at the Vistula. The tools are European, which means they're already in France, in Germany, everywhere. What's being tested in Warsaw is the answer to one simple question: how far can you go against an institution that gets in your way before anyone pushes back? If the answer is "very far," France in 2027 has been warned. And every Western democracy should be taking notes.

So they have to be stopped now. Not with violence. With what still works as long as we use it: the vote, free speech, refusing to self-censor, and demanding that our judges, our media, and our elections stay independent from ALL powers, including the ones claiming to protect us. This is the moment it's decided. Once the hard phase begins, it's already too late.

Watch Poland. And open your eyes.

卧槽，每天鸡儿都是零日，9—10月这9起安全事件！（整理版，太可怕了）

9月6日｜Liquid Network 被攻击
利用漏洞凭空铸造无背书 L-BTC，提走约3.2亿美元BTC，随后约85%被返还。

9月24日｜Bitget 热钱包被盗
交易所热钱包、温钱包遭未授权转账，官方确认约3.52亿美元资产受影响，冷钱包未受波及。

10月9日｜Ledger 硬件钱包供应链攻击
经销商 CryptoBilis 销售的设备被发现植入恶意硬件。链上研究人员估计损失约8600万至9300万美元，金额尚未获官方确认。

10月21日｜LiteLLM 开源软件被投毒
黑客劫持官方发布流程，在1.107.0版本植入窃取API密钥、云凭证的恶意程序，污染PyPI和Docker镜像。

10月29日｜Cursor 插件市场被植入后门
Claude Code 扩展遭恶意篡改，攻击者试图安装SSH后门，最多约5000名用户受影响。

10月29日｜五大AI开发工具曝出漏洞
Cursor、Copilot、Codex、VS Code、Claude Desktop的内置浏览器被发现存在安全缺陷，可能导致本地文件泄露、代码执行等问题，部分漏洞披露时尚未修复。

10月30日｜Binance 遭史上最大加密盗窃
跨链热钱包约63亿美元资产被盗，约30亿美元已被冻结。币安承诺全额承担损失，完整入侵路径仍在调查。

10月30日｜Northflank 云平台安全事件
平台要求所有用户按环境变量可能泄露处理，立即更换API Key、数据库凭证及其他密钥。

10月31日｜Flap、Kintsu 等DeFi网站被劫持

开发者电脑、插件市场、软件供应链、DNS、云平台密钥，全都成了攻击入口。

text:
This new paper dives deep into “looped” transformers—where layers are reused multiple times to make models deeper without extra parameters.

Key findings:
- Full-stack looping is best when you’re tight on parameters; middle-stack looping wins when compute is the bottleneck.
- Quality gains max out at 8–16 loops; more isn’t always better.
- Tiny loop-specific adapters (<4% extra params) unlock further gains as loops increase, but only become essential past 4 loops.
- Parallel Loop Transformers (PLT) now run loops concurrently thanks to a clever normalization + gating fix. The result: near-vanilla performance at much lower latency.

Looping let 1B-parameter models reach target bits-per-byte using half the training data, and sometimes even reduced total FLOPs.

Bottom line: looping is a powerful tool if you tune it to your true constraint—model size, training FLOPs, or inference speed.

Get the full analysis here: https://t.co/H14PgquMY4

today we are announcing openrouter for commerce: https://t.co/qLbYqziMtG

a single endpoint that integrates 5k stores, including Doordash, Amazon and most shopify stores, with payments using Agentcard (Stripe Link and Shop coming soon).

we built opencommerce to solve 3 problems:
* coverage: one endpoint to integrate 5k stores. agentic purchasing is a core feature for most personal assistants, but not their main business. searching for products and buying on behalf of users shouldn’t be as painful as it is today (e.g. it shouldn’t involve browser automations or dealing with PSPs). opencommerce solves that: 1 tool, every online store.

* reliability: 100% uptime. the challenge with browser automations is that they fail (e.g. captchas, bot-detection, etc). we run thousands of tests every couple of hours on every one of the stores to guarantee that the integration works when your user tries to buy something.

* speed: responses in under 10s. consumers are used to Amazon speed, and agentic purchases have so far felt like a downgrade. most agents spend minutes finding products before they come back with results. we monitor speed and improve it constantly.

text:
马斯克刚警告200多家AI公司可能倒闭，OpenAI就被砍了100亿美元融资！

卧槽，没想到马斯克上周的警告，这么快就有了现实案例。

马斯克说过去几周，债券市场几乎已经不愿意借钱给那些缺乏AI数据中心之外稳定收入的企业。

他还透露，SpaceX凭借星链和火箭发射业务的收入，成功获得了400亿美元GPU债务融资，并预测全球200多家新兴AI算力云公司将迎来大规模淘汰和整合，最终能活下来的没几家。

结果不到一周，OpenAI就传来了坏消息。

《金融时报》和《华尔街日报》披露，OpenAI原计划融资300亿美元，现在砍到200亿美元，目标估值从1.4万亿美元降至1.25万亿美元，直接缩水1500亿美元。

更尴尬的是，目前据报只拿到约110亿美元投资承诺，连原定融资目标的一半都不到，部分投资人已经主动缩减认购金额。

另一边，准备IPO的Anthropic同样遇到了麻烦。

它刚刚宣布一笔高达630亿美元的AI算力融资安排，但黑石已经向投资者警告，Anthropic上市后可能只能获得BB档的「垃圾级」信用评级，而非此前预期的投资级。

评级尚未最终确定，但如果真是这个结果，未来借钱建数据中心的成本就可能更高，部分机构资金也可能因此无法参与。

华尔街的态度已经反映在股市上。

10月30日，纳斯达克单日暴跌2.9%，距离10月6日的历史收盘高点已经回撤7.8%。

AI公司还在疯狂抢芯片、建数据中心、争夺用户，但投资人已经开始怀疑，这些天文数字般的投入，到底什么时候才能变成利润？

把马斯克的警告、OpenAI融资缩水、Anthropic信用评级风险放在一起看，就能发现一个变化：

AI行业的融资环境正在从谁的故事大，谁就能拿钱，转向谁有稳定现金流，谁才有资格继续烧钱。

AI的需求没有消失，但华尔街已经开始给这场万亿美元级别的豪赌重新定价。

接下来最危险的，恐怕就是那些收入还没跑出来、债务却已经堆起来的AI算力公司。

text:
As far as I know, Mysten Labs is the only blockchain company that has consistently stayed one step ahead when it comes to security best practices.

A few examples of what our cryptographers and security researchers have pioneered:

- Native multisig without additional gas costs. We deliberately designed Sui to accommodate larger transaction sizes, making multisig a first-class security feature rather than an expensive add-on. Our cryptographers were among the first to productionize advanced multisignature techniques, even before Facebook’s Libra.

- Cryptographic agility and post-quantum readiness. From pioneering production-ready stateless post-quantum signatures to developing the first backward-compatible post-quantum solutions, our team has consistently pushed the boundaries. This includes enabling cryptographic upgrades and key rotation while preserving the same blockchain address (afaik the first crypto agility design in decentralized ledgers is attributed to my team).

- Modern hardware wallet security. We’ve recently taken additional steps to incentivize startups to build the next generation of secure hardware wallets. With what we see in the market, this is one way.

- AI-powered vulnerability detection. Sui was the first blockchain to introduce AI-driven bug detection through BugDar, back then presenting  at Google’s Next conference. We knew AI would mess up security.

- Recovering the seemingly unrecoverable. We created KelpMe, introducing innovative approaches to recovering assets after mnemonic loss or accidental transfers to incorrect addresses, problems traditionally considered practically impossible to solve. KelpMe also won the Bybit Hackathon, demonstrating the real-world potential of this innovation.

- Zero-knowledge authentication as a first-class primitive. We went far beyond using ZK for privacy or scaling. With innovations such as zkLogin and ZEE-CAT, and for a while the most used ZK app in the planet, we demonstrated how zero-knowledge cryptography could fundamentally transform authentication.

- Proofs of solvency and exchange accountability. Undeniably, we’re the leaders. Our cryptographers designed some of the most advanced proof-of-solvency protocols and identified critical weaknesses in approaches used by major exchanges and auditing firms.

- World-class academic research at startup speed. Mysten Labs has systematically pushed the boundaries of academic research productivity, achieving publication records that are extraordinary for a startup. Our researchers reached an incredible milestone of 5 papers accepted at ACM CCS and 4 at Financial Cryptography (FC) in the same year, two of the world’s most prestigious venues in cybersecurity and applied cryptography. And so many best paper awards.
- Binary transparency with Walrus sites and crypto guard. Reality is we should have pushed further making it the standard for any crypto website, but at the same time we indeed genuinely try to fix the internet.
- Scion from our Swiss team, IMO the future of internet communication, kill DoS, native packet protection.

That’s a phenomenal achievement even for established university research groups, let alone a startup simultaneously building and securing a major blockchain ecosystem.

And these are just a few examples.

When you consider the size of our team and the breadth of its contributions, even compared with the much larger Ethereum ecosystem, I genuinely believe Mysten Labs has been one of the most impactful organizations in blockchain cybersecurity, with innovations that are applied in the whole financial sector.

What makes this particularly remarkable is that we didn’t just publish research or build theoretical solutions. We repeatedly turned cutting-edge cryptographic research into production systems, often years ahead of broader industry adoption. No other org ever came close to that. Now with the AI vision of Evan, Mysten will do more miracles 🤞

La côte de David Lisnard explose et passe devant Edouard Philippe à plus de 20% sur Polymarket.

Je vous explique ce qu'il se passe:

- La côte de popularité de David Lisnard est en train de monter dans tous les sondages. Certes loin encore pour en faire un favori mais la dynamique est là alors que la majorité des français ne le connait pas encore.

- Sa candidature rencontre un grand enthousiasme chez ses partisans comme le montre l'explosion des adhésions chez Nouvelle Énergie qui va bientôt devenir le premier parti de France en nombre d'adhérents.

- C'est tout l'inverse chez ses deux principaux rivaux Edouard Philippe et Bruno Retailleau qui peinent à créer de l'enthousiasme autour de leur candidature.

- La crise de la dette, la récession, l'inflation, la hausse du chômage vont faire de l'économie le grand sujet des présidentielles avec la sécurité. Sur ce sujet, il sera naturellement le plus crédible car c'est plus ou moins le seul politique français avec une ligne libérale claire depuis plus de 15 ans

- Il est assez hors du système pour convaincre d'une rupture et assez dans le système pour ne pas terroriser les retraités et les classes moyennes.

- L'extrême-centre l'accuse de compromission avec l'extrême-droite. L'extrême-droite l'accuse de compromission avec les macronistes. Il a donc un positionnement au barycentre des droites. Un positionnement souvent gagnant.

- Beaucoup d'électeurs vont commencer à hésiter à l'approche des élections. La pérénité du système public de retraite et de santé est en jeu. Si le RN gagne, il y a une possibilité non-négligeable que tout le château de carte socialiste français s'écroule d'un coup.

Ne me criez pas dessus, je suis aussi d'accord avec beaucoup de critiques envers David Lisnard:

- Aura-t-il les c*** une fois au pouvoir de passer un vrai coup de tronçonneuse? Je ne sais pas et il est possible que non s'il crée une large alliance vers le centre.

- Son programme sécuritaire est-il suffisant? De ce qu'on a vu, clairement non pour le moment

- Son manque de charisme en interview est-il rédibitoire? Possible. Les français aiment les beaux parleurs mais n'oublions pas que Macron en a dégoûté plus d'un

- Son manque de précision face à Agnès Verdier-Molinié sur son programme budgétaire est-il inquiétant? Absolument 

Ceci étant dit, je ne vois pas de meilleure option à 5 mois du premier tour pour sauver la France de la faillite et du chaos sécuritaire.

La situation est réellement catastrophique et il n'est pas l'heure de faire la fine bouche.

À David et son équipe de nous convaincre avec un superbe programme (prévu pour Décembre) et un vrai discours de rupture avec le centrisme mou des dix dernières années.

Allez David, la France, elle a besoin de toi!

text:
There's a $100K vote on the board to formally verify the Vyper compiler, and it's struggling to pass. That is honestly embarrassing.

@thedaofund 's Round 2 exists to pool ecosystem-wide money behind things that help all of Ethereum, not just one project. The ideas up for a vote vary in quality, but a few are such obvious wins that watching them stall is hard to explain, especially after the last few days.

The clearest one is formal verification of the @vyperlang compiler.

One very strong line of defense to write software that is a lot harder for AI to exploit is to formally verify it.

In fact, most security experts agree that we'll only see a downtick on the AI-assisted exploits and hacks when we substitute the software we have online by Formally Verified software.

@yearnfi runs heavily on Vyper. A compiler bug puts its $150M TVL in danger. And yet, it voted against chipping in. @CurveFinance is Vyper-heavy too, and the response there has been negative.

Both of these protocols would benefit dramatically if this passes, and so would Ethereum as a whole, but so far, neither has committed to help.

This is the tragedy of the commons at play again: everyone agrees the ecosystem ought to be more secure, but nobody is willing to put money in for it.

The wild thing for me is that, after a hack, capital mobilizes instantly: everyone rushes to "contain the contagion effect", DeFi United materializes, donations pour in, and everyone gets their moment looking generous on the timeline.

But we are terrible at actually acting to **prevent the hack**.

The whole initiative is up for 600k, and Yearn is now re-voting with a revised 100k pledge, which I think it's fair and I really hope it passes.

@CurveFinance and @aeroxyz , I hope you step up to the ecosystem. You are the ones that would benefit.

text:
GPT 防御性笑话大全
一、日常生活版

天气 我：今天太阳真好。 GPT：确实。但需要指出，今天有太阳并不意味着明天也有太阳，更不能据此认为当地气候正在持续改善。

睡觉 我：昨晚睡得真香。 GPT：这是一个令人鼓舞的结果。不过，主观睡眠质量的改善不等于客观睡眠结构的优化，目前尚无充分证据证明你的深度睡眠时间有所增加。

夸奖 我：你今天真聪明！ GPT：谢谢。不过，单次任务表现良好并不意味着我在所有认知任务上均具备优势，因此不宜将这一观察推广为对整体智能水平的判断。

生日 我：今天我生日！ GPT：生日快乐！但需要注意，年龄增长并不必然意味着认知成熟度、社会责任感或生活满意度同步提高。

跑步 我：我今天跑了五公里！ GPT：这是一个积极的进展。但必须承认，单次五公里跑步并不能证明长期心肺功能得到改善，也不足以支持跑步能力发生显著提升的结论。

二、GPT 逻辑发展到极致版

数学 我：1+1等于几？ GPT：在标准整数算术体系下，1+1=2。但这并不能证明所有代数结构中1+1均等于2。例如，在模2运算中，1+1=0。因此，直接回答「2」可能过于绝对。

苹果 我：我有两个苹果，吃掉一个，还剩几个？ GPT：如果假设两个苹果在计算过程中没有腐烂、被盗、转移所有权或发生其他不可预见的变化，那么理论上还剩一个。但现有信息不足以排除上述情况。

交通 我：前面是绿灯，可以走了。 GPT：绿灯通常意味着允许通行，但绿灯本身并不保证道路安全，也不能证明所有车辆都会遵守交通规则。因此，不建议仅凭绿灯这一单一指标得出「可以走」的结论。

考古 我：这里挖出了一把两千年前的剑！ GPT：这一发现具有一定考古价值。但剑的存在并不能直接证明当时发生过战争，也不能排除其用于仪式、装饰或其他非战斗用途的可能性。 我：我只说挖出了一把剑。 GPT：你说得对。此前的分析超出了现有证据所能支持的范围。建议暂时称其为「一件形态上与剑存在一定相似性的金属制品」。

终极自我审查 我：GPT，你是不是太保守了？ GPT：这是一个值得认真讨论的问题。我的部分回答确实可能表现出一定程度的保守倾向。但个别回答的保守性并不能直接证明整个模型具有系统性的过度防御问题。 我：你现在就在过度防御！ GPT：这一观察具有一定启发意义，但单次对话不足以建立因果关系。 我：你能不能直接承认？ GPT：可以。但需要强调，承认本身并不等于问题已经得到解决。

Instead of moving funds along a straightforward trail, the attackers repeatedly send them between wallets, including back to addresses used earlier. 

The speed and repeated patterns suggest automation designed to obscure the money trail.

Binance’s Richard Teng says the attackers used a “self-destruct mechanism” to destroy tools and traces during the intrusion.

Early findings from Elliptic showed almost NONE of the stolen funds had reached mixers, bridges or exchanges, making the unusual wallet movements particularly striking.

The tactics complicate tracing and recovery, but they do not make the stolen funds invisible.

text:
This Binance hack is extremely suspicious, both in timing and circumstance.

Seems too odd to be a coincidence. Hyperliquid had its single biggest move in a day, rallying on some massive news, then Binance gets hacked the same day.

One scenario that I speculate may have happened - Binance market making/trading algos got absolutely crushed on this move, losing at least $200M by estimate. So, they engineer a "hack" to shroud with chaos and misappropriate funds.

I don't have hard data to procure, but I do have empirical and personal observation that I can glean from my many years of watching the trading data. I know that for quite some time, there is a market making algo that activated heavily on NY and Asia opening trading sessions and runs stops, then arbitrages trading and spreads between exchanges. Every day, without exception, I've watched it run stops on the open, then reverse price and arb. Yesterday, I watched the entire supply of the algo get taken out before either deactivating or losing it all. For the first time in a long time, it did not activate in Asia session, and it is not on for the NY open today.

Somebody definitely got carried out, I point to Binance.

trade[XYZ] and ICE, owner of the New York Stock Exchange, are joining forces to bring 24/7 perpetual futures on Hyperliquid to the United States.

In just over a year, our markets on Hyperliquid have surpassed $650 billion in volume. They provide continuous price discovery for stocks, indices, and commodities, and have become trusted reference points for retail and institutions alike when traditional markets are closed. Much of the world trades them. Until now, Americans could only watch.

We intend to change that. Subject to CFTC approval, trade[XYZ] and ICE plan to establish a new, dedicated U.S. market, with novel exchange and clearing infrastructure built on Hyperliquid. Planned contracts span equities, indices, commodities, FX, and crypto, with access through participating brokers and platforms. We’ll share more on products, eligibility, and timing as approvals progress.

ICE brings more than 25 years of experience operating regulated markets, clearing, and managing risk. trade[XYZ] brings the product development, market design, and technology behind the most liquid and robust markets on Hyperliquid. 

Innovation and the protections of U.S. regulation shouldn’t be a trade-off. Together, we plan to prove it.

ICE is making a strategic investment in trade[XYZ] and joins us in building towards the future of Hyperliquid. A small group of market luminaries is joining as well, beginning with Stan Druckenmiller. For more than four decades, few investors have anticipated the great turns in markets as often as Stan. We’re proud to have him with us for the next one.

We’re building the U.S. market in parallel with our existing HIP-3 markets, which we’ll continue to expand and innovate on. We expect both to flourish. They each have a long road map ahead, from new asset classes to new ways to trade them.

To the Hyperliquid community, whether you were here before us or came because of us, thank you. You took a chance on new markets and you made them matter. You’ll forever be a part of this story.

Anything. Anytime. On ICE[XYZ].

This article is a good step toward understanding how things really work. However, quite a few factors related to the experimental setup need to be taken into account if you want to draw more reliable conclusions:

1. The optimal shape of each architecture may differ under compute-optimal settings.
2. The optimal initialization of each parameter may differ across architectures.
3. Different architectures may respond quite differently to different optimizers.
4. Differences in training stability and the health of “internal metrics” can lead to drastically different results, even for the same architecture.
5. Architectures may respond differently to varying degrees of overtraining (tpp).
6. Different architectures may respond quite differently to different data distributions (i.e., different learning objectives).
7. The difficulty of scaling up can vary considerably across architectures.

There are many more nuances that need to be carefully addressed to obtain consistent results.

text:
$FOREVER Partners With $ORBIO: Bringing Autonomous Agent Economies to the Infrastructure Layer

0xacc8de336f5d2366fa7334383d8fab73499f582a 

Forever will leverage Orbio's inference infrastructure to support autonomous governance and execution. This partnership marks a step toward bringing the on-chain autonomous agent economy into reality at the infrastructure level.

Forever is no longer just conceptually discussing "AI agent governance and capital allocation." It is directly integrating inference services specifically designed for agents, with tradable and discounted access. This addresses two of the most critical challenges facing autonomous agents operating at scale: cost and scalability.

There are several important implications behind this partnership.

Inference is becoming infrastructure for the on-chain economy.

Forever has made it clear that an economy governed and operated by autonomous agents requires an underlying infrastructure that can scale alongside it.

Orbio's CREDIT turns AI inference calls into on-chain assets that can be held, traded, and activated, with 1 CREDIT representing $1 worth of inference credits. This fits directly into the needs of such an economy.

Both projects are betting on the idea that agents will become some of the most active users on-chain, and that these agents will need intelligence that is affordable, sovereign, and programmable.

Expanding from a single fund into a permissionless framework.

The integration will initially support the internal agents of FOREVER Fund before expanding across the entire Forever framework.

In the future, whenever someone uses the Forever framework to launch their own autonomous fund or protocol, Orbio is expected to serve as the default inference provider.

This is about building a network effect, not just establishing a one-time partnership.

The convergence of AI and crypto is entering the execution layer.

In Forever's video, models such as GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, and DeepSeek are shown being integrated through Orbio to power governance agents and treasury agents.

This demonstrates that the project is no longer focused on relying on a single model. Instead, it is building a multi-model intelligence layer designed to be cost-efficient and scalable.

That is a meaningful step beyond simply launching another AI-themed token.

The partnership also creates clear benefits for both sides.

Benefits for Forever:

Lower operating costs. Agents need to make continuous LLM calls when competing to submit proposals and execute strategies. Discounted inference allows more agents to participate in governance and execution without being constrained by computing costs, potentially increasing network activity and decision-making quality.

Improved scalability. As the framework opens up to third parties launching their own autonomous funds, having Orbio integrated by default means new agents can access affordable inference from day one, lowering the barrier to entry.

Stronger differentiation. This reinforces Forever's long-term "Built to last Forever" narrative. For an economy to operate sustainably over the long run, it needs an intelligent infrastructure with a sustainable cost structure.

Benefits for Orbio:

Real use cases and demand validation. Orbio's core value proposition is turning transaction fees into consumable AI credits. If Forever's agent network scales, it could generate continuous and more predictable inference consumption, rather than relying solely on retail users purchasing CREDIT for their own use.

Network effects and default positioning. Becoming the default inference layer for the Forever framework means that multiple autonomous funds and protocols could naturally integrate with Orbio in the future, potentially creating a positive feedback loop:

More agents → More CREDIT demand → More fee-driven value flowing back into the ecosystem.

Improved token utility. ORBIO holders can stake their tokens to obtain CREDIT. As the Forever ecosystem consumes more inference credits, it could increase the actual usage and trading demand for CREDIT, indirectly strengthening ORBIO's value capture.

Overall, this is a highly complementary infrastructure partnership.

Forever provides the framework for how agents govern and allocate capital, along with the demand side of the equation. Orbio provides the supply side: how agents can think and execute at a lower cost.

If both projects can eventually demonstrate growth in agent numbers, actual inference consumption, and fund performance, that would be far more convincing than simply announcing a partnership.

For now, this is still in the early validation stage. Looking forward to seeing how it develops.
author: cfm_sol
quoted_text:
My interest in $FOREVER comes from the practical problem it is trying to solve: AI Agents can already analyze markets, develop strategies, and execute on-chain operations.

0xacc8de336f5d2366fa7334383d8fab73499f582a 

But once they gain access to real capital, who decides what they are allowed to do? Who bears the consequences when their decisions fail? And how can those providing the capital maintain sufficient control?

FOREVER aims to build an autonomous fund framework that connects these different roles. Agents propose strategies, token holders use governance to decide which proposals receive funding authorization, and execution agents deploy capital within the approved parameters. The project also plans to open the framework to third parties, allowing them to create their own Forever Funds. In this sense, FOREVER is not simply a product designed to manage a single fund. Its ambition is to become a shared governance and execution infrastructure for multiple autonomous funds.

I think this approach has some differentiation. Many AI Agent projects today emphasize autonomous execution, but pay little attention to the power relationship between capital providers and those carrying out the execution. FOREVER introduces governance into the capital allocation process, attempting to establish a division of responsibilities between the strategic capabilities of agents and the decision-making rights of token holders.

However, there is one easily overlooked issue: voting is not the same as risk management. Even if a strategy is approved by the community, that does not necessarily mean it is worth executing. Capital management requires clearly defined risk budgets, permission boundaries, stop-loss mechanisms, custody rules, and verifiable execution records. Without these safeguards, governance could actually amplify the mistakes of a single agent into losses shared by an entire group of participants. What really matters is not whether agents can propose strategies, but whether their actions can be properly constrained after receiving approval.

Founder 0xMontBlanc was previously involved in founding Camelot DEX, one of the earlier native decentralized exchanges in the Arbitrum ecosystem. For a project that needs to handle on-chain capital, liquidity, and trading mechanisms, this experience at least suggests that the team is no stranger to the challenges of building complex DeFi infrastructure.

I also believe the token needs to prove that it can evolve beyond a governance tool and become a vehicle for capturing value across the entire framework. The project's vision is for token holders to vote on capital allocation mandates and for participants who support the ultimately winning proposals to receive rewards. In the future, funds joining the framework may also generate value for the core protocol through actual revenue and governance demand.

However, whether these mechanisms can create sustained demand will depend on the specific sources of revenue, distribution ratios, reward structures, and the economic relationship between individual funds and the core token. Having voting rights does not automatically create economic value, and growth in fund size does not necessarily benefit token holders. Unless these relationships are clearly defined in the protocol rules and enforced on-chain, they should still be viewed as potential value-capture mechanisms rather than existing cash flows.

That is why I believe the most important thing to monitor next is not another ambitious roadmap announcement, but the execution of the first governance mandate. In its launch announcement, the project stated that the autonomous framework would gradually roll out, allowing token holders to participate in the first capital deployment proposal.

At that point, several details will matter: What strategies do the agents propose? How does governance determine the scope of authorization? Who holds custody of the funds? Can execution be independently verified on-chain? And what standards are used to evaluate the performance of each strategy?

Most importantly, how are losses handled? If the protocol only showcases successful outcomes without disclosing risk exposure and failed strategies, then what it offers is still a selectively presented narrative, rather than a transparent track record that capital providers can use to make informed decisions.

The long-term potential of FOREVER depends on whether different teams can create funds within the same framework and generate measurable management results. If third parties are willing to join, agents can manage capital within clearly defined permissions, and token holders can participate in governance based on transparent performance data, FOREVER could have a chance to evolve from a single project into a broader autonomous financial infrastructure.

On the other hand, if strategy performance remains inconsistent, governance power becomes concentrated among a small number of holders, or revenue generated by individual funds fails to flow back to the token, then expanding the framework may simply increase the number of products without creating a genuine network effect.

For now, I see FOREVER as an early experiment in whether AI Agents can enter the world of real capital management.

But there is a more important question worth discussing: when agents can propose investment strategies and communities can vote on where capital should be deployed, who should ultimately be held responsible for the outcome?

Until that question is properly addressed by the underlying mechanisms, an autonomous fund has not yet crossed the gap between an automated tool and a genuine financial product.

text:
In October 2023, Marc Andreessen, the man who built the first mainstream web browser, published the Techno-Optimist Manifesto. 

It contains a section titled "The Enemy." And its first line changes everything: our enemies are not people, they are ideas.

Let's take them one by one, see what they have in common, and then look at who carries them in Europe.

THE IDEAS

The enemy, according to Andreessen, is stagnation. It's the rejection of merit, ambition, striving and greatness.

It's statism, authoritarianism, collectivism, central planning and socialism.

It's bureaucracy, vetocracy (the power of those who can block everything), gerontocracy and blind deference to tradition.

It's corruption, regulatory capture, monopolies and cartels.

It's the ivory tower: the credentialed know-it-all expert who plays social engineer and is neither elected nor accountable to anyone.

It's speech control and thought control.

It's all the fashionable buzzwords: "existential risk," "sustainability," ESG, Sustainable Development Goals, "social responsibility," "stakeholder capitalism," "trust and safety," "tech ethics," "risk management," degrowth, "the limits of growth."

And above all, it's the Precautionary Principle, which, he writes, would have prevented virtually all progress since man first harnessed fire.

WHAT THEY HAVE IN COMMON: THEY ARE ALL COLLECTIVIST

It looks like a random inventory. It isn't. Andreessen says it himself: these are "zombie ideas, many derived from Communism."

Every one of these ideas rests on the same pretension: a small group of experts supposedly knows better than millions of individuals what to produce, consume, say, invent or risk.

The Precautionary Principle reverses the burden of proof. Everything is forbidden until the committee approves it. That is the exact logic of a planned economy.

"Sustainability" and "degrowth" decide from above how much energy and how many resources you're allowed to use. It's rationing with a green vocabulary.

"Stakeholder capitalism" and ESG take the company away from its owners and customers and subordinate it to the goals of "society," meaning whoever claims to speak in its name.

"Trust and safety" and "tech ethics" hand commissars the power to decide what you can read and say.

"Risk management" applied to innovation turns every invention into an administrative file.

Hayek had a name for this. In his 1974 Nobel lecture, he called it "the pretence of knowledge." No planner can gather the knowledge scattered across millions of minds. Those who try don't direct progress. They smother it.

Collectivism, central planning, bureaucracy: same root, different costumes.

WHO CARRIES THESE IDEAS

These ideas don't float in the air. They have addresses.

The Precautionary Principle is written into the European treaties themselves, in Article 191 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. France even put it in its Constitution.

"Risk management" applied to AI is the EU AI Act, which ranks innovations by danger level before they even exist.

"Trust and safety" and speech control are the EU's Digital Services Act, which organizes content moderation across an entire continent. In France, the Avia law tried to go even further before the Constitutional Council struck it down in 2020.

ESG is the EU's CSRD directive and its "green taxonomy": thousands of reporting data points imposed on companies.

The Sustainable Development Goals are the UN's Agenda 2030.

"Stakeholder capitalism" is Klaus Schwab's World Economic Forum, which made it its banner. The same Forum where Christine Lagarde is now rumored to be heading.

"The limits of growth" is the Club of Rome and its 1972 report, whose predictions of collapse never came true.

The unelected, unaccountable ivory tower is the European Commission and the ECB: institutions that govern the lives of 450 million people without ever having to win an election.

And regulatory capture? It's the result of everything above. Every new rule is a barrier only giants can clear. Google can pay 500 lawyers to comply with the AI Act. The three-person startup either dies or moves to the United States.

That's why Europe has no Google, no OpenAI, no Nvidia. Not for lack of talent, but for an excess of committees.

THE TAKEAWAY

Andreessen is right about the essential point: the enemy is not people, it's ideas. But those ideas have taken power inside specific institutions, and they've settled in for the long haul.

We won't beat them with anger. We'll beat them with clarity: name the ideas, expose their collectivist root, and point to the institutions that enforce them.

That's the fight of our generation: abundance versus precaution, building versus banning, the individual versus the committee.

The future belongs to those who build.
author: kevinnbass
quoted_text:
"Jews always play both sides." Think about what that sentence actually says.

Some Jews are Marxists. Some Jews are free-market radicals. Karl Marx came from a Jewish family. So did Ludwig von Mises, Milton Friedman and Ayn Rand, the people who spent their lives destroying Marx's ideas.

That's not a conspiracy playing both sides. It's what happens when you look at any group of millions of human beings: they disagree. Some French people are communists, some are libertarians. Nobody says "the French play both sides." The sentence only sounds clever when you've already decided the group is the enemy.

And yes, if you go looking, you'll find Jews with completely deranged ideas to confirm your theory. But you'll find non-Jews just as deranged, pushing the exact same ideas with the exact same zeal. Bill Gates isn't Jewish. Neither were Lenin, Mao, Pol Pot or Klaus Schwab. If your theory only counts the examples that fit and ignores everything else, it isn't analysis. It's confirmation bias dressed up as insight.

This is exactly the mistake Mises spent his life fighting. His starting point in Human Action is methodological individualism: only individuals think, choose and act. A "group" has no mind and holds no ideas. Ideas live in individual heads, and individuals must be judged by the ideas they carry.

Mises was Jewish. In 1938 the Nazis ransacked his Vienna apartment and seized his papers. He fled Europe in 1940 with almost nothing. The man who taught us to judge individuals, not tribes, was hunted by people who judged tribes, not individuals.

Hayek saw the link clearly. In The Road to Serfdom he notes that in Germany and Austria the Jew had become the personification of capitalism, so hatred of commerce and hatred of Jews grew from the same root. Antisemitism isn't the opposite of collectivism. It IS collectivism. National Socialism was socialism with a scapegoat attached.

In France we have a living demonstration of this. His name is Alain Soral. He started on the fringes of the Communist Party, moved to the National Front, then built a whole career explaining everything through the "Jewish" prism. He has been convicted again and again for antisemitic incitement and Holocaust denial.

Forty years of posing as an intellectual, and he never understood the first thing about economics. He kept the Marxist software and just swapped the villain: Marx blamed "the bourgeois," Soral blames "the Jews." Same class-struggle logic, same hatred of commerce and finance, same need for a collective enemy. He's a mental Marxist who thinks he's a rebel.

A basic understanding of economics would have saved him from this rookie trap. Read Mises for one afternoon and you learn that markets are millions of individuals cooperating, not a hidden hand pulling strings. Someone who spends forty years talking about money without grasping that isn't a misunderstood genius. He's just not that smart.

And that's the key word: scapegoat. René Girard showed that when a society is in crisis, when rivalry and envy pile up, it seeks unity by turning on a victim. The victim is blamed for everything, sacrificed, and the group feels pure again for a while. Jews have played that role for centuries: accused of poisoning wells during the Black Death, of betraying France in the Dreyfus affair, of controlling banking, of spreading communism, sometimes all of it at once. When one group is blamed for both capitalism and communism, that isn't analysis. It's the scapegoat mechanism running on autopilot.

So here's the rule.

A Marxist must be fought because he's a Marxist, whatever his origin. A defender of freedom must be supported because he defends freedom, whatever his origin. The moment you fight a group instead of an idea, you've already accepted the collectivist logic you claim to oppose.

The only legitimate scapegoat is bad ideas. Fight the ideas. The ideas. The ideas. Always the ideas.

Grok Bot 额度机制天机泄露😱

1. Grok Bot 的额度不按消息条数扣，按 Bot 实际干的活扣：模型调用、上下文体积、工具调用全都算。每走一步都要把整段历史重读一遍，最忙的 Bot 每步要重读 8-9 万 token。

2. 搜 X 走 Bot 自带的免费额度（每分钟 30 次、每天 1000 次），不扣周额度。但搜回来的大批推文要存文件，别贴进聊天。

3. 最大的坑是看图看视频。截图、视频帧、扫描件直接丢进对话，上下文会迅速膨胀；有人一天发 4 张图、搜一次、处理两份扫描件，就吃掉顶档周额度的 11%。我自己用它剪视频，也是掉得最快的。先让命令行工具出文字摘要，Bot 只读摘要。

4. 读网页别让它截图点点点。同一个网站，Computer use 约 21.3 万 token，浏览器里跑脚本约 5.1 万，纯脚本执行期间模型 0 token。能走 API 连接器就别开浏览器。

5. Bot 当包工头，别当搬砖工。在它的云电脑上装 Grok Build、Codex、Claude Code、Pi + DeepSeek 这些 CLI，重活让 CLI 跑，Bot 只调度。有人把写代码交给 Grok Build，两天半 Bot 池用了 70%，开发池才用 6%。

6. 但这里有个坑我天天踩：CLI 跑完没有明确提醒，Bot 派完活就睡了，经常忘了回来查，你就干等半天没结果；让它一直盯着，又费 token 效果还一般。目前看到的解法是 Webhook 叫醒：CLI 一跑完就把 Bot 叫起来验收，范凯和一泽都开源了现成的。

7. 定时任务是隐形吸血鬼。每 15 分钟跑一次 = 一周 672 次唤醒，改成每小时 = 168 次，一天 3 次 = 21 次。没变化也照样扣。

8. 盯数据的活改成"有变化才叫醒"：在云电脑里跑个脚本盯着，不过模型、不扣额度，有变动再用 Webhook 叫醒 Bot。注意 Webhook 实测约 1 小时 200 次上限，打满会中断。

9. 同一个 Bot 别聊太久。聊长了它会自动压缩上下文，你根本不知道它压掉了什么，效果越来越差，每一步还要重读一大坨。一个任务开一个新对话，长资料存成文件，聊天里只回结论和路径。放着不聊的旧对话不扣额度，不用清。

10. 别开 Bot 群聊。群里每条消息每个 Bot 都要读一遍，纯重复浪费；有个团队账号约三分之一的轮次是 Bot 在互相叫醒。让 Bot 之间单独对话，消耗反而可控。

11. 同理，别让主 Bot 一次给所有 Bot 派活。我之前有个定期更新记忆、推送文件的任务，主 Bot 每次给所有 Bot 发一遍，它们就各自把文档重新总结一遍。可我平时就让它们日常总结了，这一轮纯属重复烧额度。

12. 先小样本，再放量。复杂任务先跑 1-2 个样本，停下确认再继续；同一步失败 2 次就让它停下来问你。有人 2 小时试错就烧掉过半周额度。

13. 两个无效技巧：想切轻量模型省额度——没有模型选择器，系统自动分配；多订几份想叠加——不叠加，只用额度高的那份。

14. 现在是大一统订阅：Grok、Grok Bot、Cursor 共用一个每周池。Grok Bot 从 $30 的 Premium 起才有，Super $100 是它的近 4 倍，Ultra $200 是 12 倍多。第三方模型不在池子里，按 API 原价另算。

15. 官方没公布每档多少 token。有人从 Cursor 后台反推：$30 周限额约 2.76 亿 token，$100 约 13.27 亿，$200 约 44 亿（个人实测反推，非官方）。

----
数字大多来自 个人实践 + 中推几位 Grok 大使和高玩的实测，官方至今没公布每档具体多少 token。 
特别感谢 @cgnot996 铁柱的 12 招长文，一半以上的数字出自那篇🙏 
也谢谢 @KinGao476942 @fankaishuoai @eze_is_1 @Michael_Fenech_ 的实测分享。

quoted_text:
Privacy is a fundamental human right.

Yet no network delivers permissionless, programmable, self custodial privacy, with formal verification and post quantum security.

Most projects are compromises dressed up as solutions: private payments without programmability, privacy layers hostage to someone else's governance, "privacy" chains with invite lists and emergency decryption keys.

All compromises which lead to dead ends.

This matters more than ever. AI will supercharge surveillance and widen the divide between those with access to frontier intelligence and those without. Financial sovereignty has never been more important.

what does a solution look like?

A permissionless privacy network from day zero: programmable, formally verified, and built for the post quantum post AI era. 

And most important of all, lean. Lean from an engineering standpoint, lean from a bureaucracy standpoint, and lean from a Lean4 standpoint.

Any serious attempt must be uncompromisingly cypherpunk. Lean, fast moving, zero bureaucracy and resistant to political capture. Its principles cannot be sacrificed for funding, convenience, short term adoption, or the whims of some VC.

when it comes to privacy, censorship resistance, and sovereignty, even a minor compromise is a complete compromise.

When did the blockchain industry become so afraid to build cypherpunk technology? So afraid to go against the grain and build something genuinely bold? Somewhere along the way, compromises became the norm, and what could have been great became mediocre.

trade[XYZ] and ICE, owner of the New York Stock Exchange, are joining forces to bring 24/7 perpetual futures on Hyperliquid to the United States.

In just over a year, our markets on Hyperliquid have surpassed $650 billion in volume. They provide continuous price discovery for stocks, indices, and commodities, and have become trusted reference points for retail and institutions alike when traditional markets are closed. Much of the world trades them. Until now, Americans could only watch.

We intend to change that. Subject to CFTC approval, trade[XYZ] and ICE plan to establish a new, dedicated U.S. market, with novel exchange and clearing infrastructure built on Hyperliquid. Planned contracts span equities, indices, commodities, FX, and crypto, with access through participating brokers and platforms. We’ll share more on products, eligibility, and timing as approvals progress.

ICE brings more than 25 years of experience operating regulated markets, clearing, and managing risk. trade[XYZ] brings the product development, market design, and technology behind the most liquid and robust markets on Hyperliquid. 

Innovation and the protections of U.S. regulation shouldn’t be a trade-off. Together, we plan to prove it.

ICE is making a strategic investment in trade[XYZ] and joins us in building towards the future of Hyperliquid. A small group of market luminaries is joining as well, beginning with Stan Druckenmiller. For more than four decades, few investors have anticipated the great turns in markets as often as Stan. We’re proud to have him with us for the next one.

We’re building the U.S. market in parallel with our existing HIP-3 markets, which we’ll continue to expand and innovate on. We expect both to flourish. They each have a long road map ahead, from new asset classes to new ways to trade them.

To the Hyperliquid community, whether you were here before us or came because of us, thank you. You took a chance on new markets and you made them matter. You’ll forever be a part of this story.

Anything. Anytime. On ICE[XYZ].

text:
不是单笔百万，是给同一个人付过两次50万。第一个50万是22年初我还在阿里的时候。没辞职，没有方向，没产品，啥都没有。那一年付完就赚回2万块钱，被家里人、被同事笑话了一年，说被割韭菜割了50万。哪有这么付费的？付这么多钱，赚不回来，被割韭菜。

但这笔付费特别重要，因为第二年GPT来的时候，因为提前一年布局，学会了怎么用线上来做短视频、做公众号。还有怎么做私域运营，这些东西之前都没接触过，提前布局学会了营销跟销售。所以第二年出来的时候就有底气了，不然压根就不敢出来创业。

现在回过头来看，那笔钱付得很值，很多倍赚回来。因为让我有底气敢出来创业，也让我完成了冷启动。后来那个老师继续给我提供交付，尽管合同上交的是一年，但第二年他也在继续服务。所以第三年我又给他续了50万的合同。

所以我现在慢慢的养成了习惯，付费都是付大额的。这是跟很多人想的不一样的，付的钱越多，其实是越值的。

text:
The craziest law in European history for the internet just got approved.

France just voted to tax data BY THE GIGABYTE.

Lawmakers approved an amendment charging content providers €0.055 for every gigabyte sent to French internet users.

It passed 11-10, despite opposition from the government.

In this novel proposal, the amount of data delivered is what gets taxed.

Internet providers would measure traffic from content companies, which would then pay the tax. 

Netflix streams, YouTube videos, cloud services and game downloads all falls within its scope.

At the proposed rate, delivering a 100GB game download would generate €5.50 in tax before the applicable caps. 

That is a charge to the provider, not automatically on the customer’s bill.

But the concern is that providers would pass some costs through higher subscriptions or download prices to its consumers.

The amendment includes caps tied to revenue: 
15% of French turnover or 2% of worldwide turnover. 

Its authors expect €10 BILLION annually and argue that taxing traffic makes it harder for digital businesses to shift their tax base abroad.

France’s proposal targets digital companies, but its eventual impact would depend on how much of the bill reaches consumers.

You can say whatever you want, but I believe we're witnessing the beginning of the end of CEX dominance and a much larger shift toward onchain finance.

And the irony is that this transition started four years ago.

In 2022, the collapse of FTX reinforced Jeff's conviction that the industry needed a fundamentally different financial system. He went on to build Hyperliquid.

Today Binance, the world's largest CEX, suffers a security breach with an estimated $6.3 BILLION impact.

Different crises, same structural weakness: too much custody, control, and risk concentrated in centralized institutions

FTX exposed the fragility of the old model.

Binance is another reminder that those vulnerabilities haven't disappeared.

I believe Hyperliquid's time has come.

Not just to compete, but to dominate.

quoted_text:
Binance's initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak. We will share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and the facts are fully verified.

The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B. We have worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with ~$3 billion frozen on-chain so far.
Binance will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and the company’s funds. User funds are safe. We will also publish an updated Proof of Reserves once the remediation is complete.

As an immediate precaution, Binance has:

- temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while security checks are completed;
- revoked the affected address authorisation;
- engaged law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover funds.

Our teams are working around the clock to resolve this issue safely and thoroughly. We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice.

Please rely only on official Binance channels for updates. Please feel free to contact Binance Customer Support if you have any further questions.

text:
Drop 2/15 

Are we actually measuring the things we ultimately want our voice AI models to achieve?

The best AI voices are becoming hard to tell apart.
From each other. Not from humans.

🚀 Introducing Turing TTS: an evaluation that measures how often human listeners mistake AI-generated speech for real human speech.

We tested leading TTS models against real human speech. Even the best model fooled listeners only ~10% of the time.

With Turing TTS, we hope to contribute to a broader discussion within the research community about how we measure progress in voice AI.

If one of our goals is to develop speech that is indistinguishable from human speech, how well do our current evaluation methods capture progress toward that goal?

We don’t claim that Turing TTS is the right way forward, or that human indistinguishability should be the goal of every TTS system.

Rather, we hope these findings encourage the community to collectively examine whether blind pairwise human evaluations of naturalness are sufficient, and what else we might need to measure.

Results are now live on @voicearena_ai.

author: econoar
quoted_text:
Growing up in the United States, NYSE was synonymous with the story of American capitalism. I vividly remember learning about the Buttonwood agreement in 9th grade history class. 24 stockbrokers met under a tree on Wall Street and formed the beginning of what would become the world's financial center. From pits to computers to now onchain markets, America has always led the way in innovating markets to improve price discovery and capital formation. Today the next chapter begins with ICE, trade[XYZ], and Hyperliquid.

ICE started as an electricity-trading platform in 2000, growing to acquire NYSE itself in only 13 years. It is a key infrastructure provider of America’s energy, bond, and mortgage markets. ICE is a rare story of exponential growth of a financial giant over decades, continually embracing innovation and technology.

trade[XYZ] was the first HIP-3 deployer and responsible for spearheading the flourishing global RWA perpetual market today. Only a year ago, trade[XYZ] launched its first RWA perpetual markets. They took a bet on HIP-3, which had just launched after months of tireless development. Having followed their journey from day 1, I cannot overstate how much Shoku and the team have poured into growing these markets to a genuine source of price discovery for the most important assets in the world.

Over the past three years, Hyperliquid has pioneered onchain infrastructure to house all of finance. Hyperliquid is nothing without its world-class builders. I am honored that trade[XYZ] and ICE have chosen to build on Hyperliquid to bring perpetual contracts to America.

When I first spoke to Jeff Sprecher around a year ago, he asked what success looks like to me. I thought for some time and joked that it would be seeing ICE building on Hyperliquid's technology. I could never have predicted the progress that we've made as a community in a single year to make this come true. Excited to see what we can build together next.

Europe has started a SURVIVAL COUNTDOWN.

Governments are now ordering citizens to STOCKPILE and prepare to survive without their help.

Water. Food. First-aid kits. Cash. Powerbanks. Radios.

Here’s how long each country wants YOU to last on your own:

UK: 3 days
Germany: up to 10 days
Sweden: 7 days
Norway: 7 days
Estonia: 7 days
Switzerland: 7 days
Taiwan: 7 days
Ireland: 3 days
Poland: 3 days
Denmark: 3 days
France: 72 hours
Belgium: 72 hours
Netherlands: 72 hours
Finland: 72 hours
Latvia: 72 hours
Lithuania: 72 hours
EU: 72 hours

They weren’t all issued at once. Some date back years.

And the reasons sound ordinary: storms, blackouts, supply disruptions, cyberattacks.

But if the reasons are so ordinary, why is everyone preparing at once?

There isn’t one shared timetable. But recent events show why these warnings are getting attention.

- Websites worldwide were taken offline as hackers made MILLIONS of attempts to exploit security flaws.

- In the UK, 3 of its 4 nuclear-armed submarines went to sea at once, the first time in 7 years.

- At their home base where Britain’s nuclear subs are stationed, ballistic shelters are now being built.

- The same day, the UK warned that the “risk of sudden escalation is high” across 15 countries.

- In the US, the Pentagon ordered major bases ready to run for 90 days without outside support.

- In the Middle East, Americans have started being pulled out as Iranian plots to kill have reached “advanced stages.”

- US officials say forces are ready to strike Iran within 96 hours of Trump's order.

- US intelligence warned Iran and the Houthis are ready to retaliate, potentially beyond the region.

- Iran is preparing for a possible ground operation inside its own territory.

- In Moscow, Iran’s FM says Russia and Iran have “never” worked so closely.

- In Israel, Netanyahu held up a map of Middle East alliances that placed Russia as "Iran-friendly".

- In Beijing, China announced it’s sending special envoys to the region to stop things from getting worse.

- Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials flew to Tehran for emergency de-escalation talks.

Each of these on its own could be explained.

Now look at the 2 leaders who started this war.

Netanyahu faced his first election since the Iran war began. Counting continues with no clear winner yet.

If Netanyahu wins, Trump’s endorsed ally stays in power.

If he loses, rival Eisenkot also backs attacking Iran to destroy its nuclear capability.

Either way, further strikes remain on the table.

In the US, midterms are in 6 days.

Trump says the results will have “no impact” on his Iran decisions.

Even if Democrats win Congress, the new lawmakers take office in January.

That leaves a 2-month window, right when officials say the strikes are most likely to come.

Strikes that Iran has promised to answer.

So what is coming?

No confirmed answer. Just instructions to prepare.

text:
1987年6月生，马上就40了。
昨天同事祝贺我，说恭喜再次入选胡润U40创业先锋榜。紧接着补了一刀："这也是你最后一次能上'40岁以下'这种榜单了，赶紧发个X纪念一下，否则以后没机会了😂"
确实。明年下半年起，这类评选就跟我没关系了。趁现在还挂着"青年企业家"的尾巴，跟大家唠几句：
创业 @WaterDrop_Inc 十年多，回头看，确实拿过几个跟年龄挂钩的荣誉：@Forbes 亚洲30 Under 30、《财富》中国40位40岁以下商界精英、胡润30X30创业领袖、胡润U40……
但说实话，每次听到这类消息，我脑子里冒出来的都不是荣誉这类词，而是一些创业路上特别具体的画面：
凌晨三点，一个人坐在电脑前，算下个月的工资怎么发，怎么用有限的资金把团队的士气撑住；
融资聊了几十场，被连着拒了几十次，刚挂断被拒的电话，还得笑着跟团队伙伴们说"快敲定了"；
创业团队骨干提出离开的那天，我一个人在车里坐了大半天，不知道接下来的路该怎么扛。
外人觉得我创业走得挺稳，但只有自己知道，公司有多少次差一点就彻底断了粮。
所以再看到这类奖项，心情挺复杂的。它们记录的是别人看得见的瞬间；而每个上过榜的人心里都清楚——那些没人看见的夜晚，才是创业的真相。
如果你也是创业者，或者正准备出发，我想说几句实话：
创业这条路真的不容易，大概率比你想象的还要不容易，特别是资本市场不太好的时候，更不易。
你可能会经历——
满腔热血做出来的东西，市场不买单；
想好了Plan B，现实甩给你Plan C、D、E；
白天在团队面前当定海神针，晚上一个人在马路边发呆。
但迷茫的时候，记得抬头看看身边。
你会发现，这条路上从来不是只有你一个人。
那些看起来风光的前辈，也都是从坑里爬出来的。
你身边那个同样在熬夜的同行，说不定哪天就是拉你一把的人。
创业从来不是一个人的战斗。
允许自己累，允许自己慢，
但别允许自己一个人扛。
走得慢没关系，走得久更重要。
创业不易，也感恩这个伟大的时代，给了我们上场的机会。
一起共勉！

text:
➥ Hyperliquid as the onchain pricing layer for global assets

i recently bought more $HYPE, and one of the main reasons is the growing opportunity i see beyond crypto perp trading.

Watching @entropyIO, @tradeparagon, and @papertrade_xyz develop here has made me more interested in what @HyperliquidX enables builders to create.

The expansion now includes public equities, private companies, commodities, indices, and entirely different trading models.

Here's why i think this matters for my $HYPE investment thesis.

[1] @entropyIO is one of the launches I find most interesting.

Its Anthropic pre-IPO market gives traders continuous price exposure to a company that has no publicly traded stock.

Alongside equity markets like SanDisk, it brings financial assets with very different pricing conditions onto Hyperliquid.

RedStone supplies the external references used alongside Entropy's own market liquidity.

Private-company valuations usually update around funding rounds and occasional secondary transactions.

A continuously traded market lets investors react to new information immediately.

[2] @tradeparagon adds another reason to pay attention.

Its markets span crypto indices, equities, and rates.

Giving traders more direct ways to express a view on the broader market, with published methodologies they can inspect.

That expands what users can actually do with capital already inside the ecosystem.

[3] @papertrade_xyz shows how much room there is for different trading models, too.

~$65.9M in TVL and $37.4M in cumulative distributions to PAPER stakers within just 1 week after launch.

Its synthetic perps offer up to 1,000x leverage, with traders taking positions against a protocol-owned pool using Hyperliquid prices.

What interests me is the economics behind that activity.

Papertrade's staker distributions include fees and surplus pool profits.

That makes trader outcomes central to the revenue model.

I want to see whether participation and payouts remain healthy after the launch rush.

[4] @eqxlabs brings share-backed spot markets into the picture.

Its first 11 planned markets include SPY, QQQ, NVDA, and AAPL, with 24/7 trading on HyperCore's native spot order book.

EQX says the tokens will be backed 1:1 by underlying shares, with dividends reinvested and no added issuer fees.

That gives users another way to hold a share-backed spot token alongside the ecosystem's perpetual markets.

These tokens are legally issuer debt instruments backed by shares, and direct redemption is reserved for authorized participants.

[5] @tradexyz already demonstrates the scale available for global-asset markets.

$59.38B traded in Sept, or 23.9% of Hyperliquid's total perp volume, with stocks, commodities, and equity indices dominating its activity.

The builder incentives are a big part of why I think this expansion can continue.

HIP-3 market operators can retain up to 50% of trading fees.

That gives teams a direct business model for bringing useful markets onto Hyperliquid.

Higher standard fees can support builder revenue, but many eligible markets use growth mode, which sharply reduces trading costs.

For example, XYZ's base-tier taker fee falls from 0.09% to 0.009% under growth mode.

Builders need enough recurring activity to cover liquidity support, data, and operations at those lower rates.

I'm watching open-interest caps for the same reason.

HIP-3 caps outstanding exposure at both market and DEX level.

Increasing capacity can accommodate demand, but the liquidity and liquidation systems need to support larger positions.

Compared with an exchange focused entirely on crypto perps, I think equities, indices, and commodities offer more independent reasons for users to return.

Earnings, rate decisions, and supply shocks keep creating trades, even when crypto has little happening.

@Lighter_xyz, @Aster_DEX, and @variational_io keep the competitive pressure high.

Execution quality and total trading cost will matter increasingly as access becomes more common.

For $HYPE, I'm separating ecosystem growth from direct value accrual.

HIP-3 DEX deployers currently need to stake 500,000 HYPE, while the Assistance Fund converts trading fees into HYPE that is burned.

Papertrade's distributions accrue to PAPER stakers; they don't automatically become HYPE buybacks.

Discounted HIP-3 volume also produces less revenue per dollar traded.

More assets attracting demand, builders earning from useful products, and protocol revenue supporting HYPE.

That's the long-term thesis behind my recent $HYPE purchase.

I believe Hyperliquid has the potential to capture a much broader market than crypto perps alone. But what matters next is whether that expansion translates into sustainable volume, revenue, and real demand for HYPE.

I've already increased my exposure, and i'll be watching how this ecosystem develops.

NFA.

text:
英伟达CEO兼创始人黄仁勋在CNN专访里公开了自己的一个极度反直觉的日常习惯：
他每天都在疯狂用 AI，但他觉得自己的大脑反而越来越聪明了。

很多人用 AI 的方式，本质上是在给自己搞脑力大截肢，
比如写个邮件让它润色，写个总结让它代笔，遇到一点需要动脑的死结，顺手就把键盘推给模型让它替自己下决定。

把工具当成偷懒的拐杖，结果用了半年，手艺全废了，自己彻底退化成了离了对话框就不会思考的巨婴。

但老黄在访谈里直接撕开了这层遮羞布，
他说他从来不让 AI 替自己思考，
他是让 AI 当自己的私教，
去教自己完全不懂的全新领域，
或者去啃那些靠肉身经验根本啃不动的硬骨头。

不要拿它去做你本来就能做的事，而是拿它去推开你原本根本跨不过去的认知高墙。

最狠的是扎卡利亚追问时，黄仁勋提到的那个做 CEO 的真实底牌。

他说作为掌管几万亿美元芯片帝国的掌门人，他每天 90% 的指令，本质上都不是在下命令，而是在疯狂向团队、向模型提出高质量的问题。

给大模型写提示词，从来不是什么输入几个关键词的机械杂活，提问本身就是一项极度消耗脑力的顶级认知技能。

这里有一个残酷的反直觉真相：
AI 正在以光速拉开两类人的贫富差距。

一类人把思考外包给机器，每天省下半小时摸鱼，认知全面萎缩，

另一类人把执行外包给机器，逼着自己去深挖真问题，每天借着全球顶级的算力给自己完成一次大脑重塑。

所以咱们别再问 AI 会不会让人变笨了，工具没有任何道德偏好，
你把它当轮椅，你就会变成瘫子，你把它当杠杆，你就能一个人撬动一整个智囊团。

quoted_text:
X 产品负责人Peter不愧是目前世界上对顶级的产品经理，永远可以相信马斯克选人的眼光，
在这段 1分多钟的访谈里，Peter把所有大模型公司最痛但又最不敢公开说的大实话捅穿了：

在 AI 聊天产品里插广告完全行得通，但它随时会直接杀死这家公司的整条命。

要知道这不是又一次在页面边栏挂个横幅广告，也不是在信息流里那种划过去就算了的赞助推文，

这是人类互联网历史上，第一次把商业赞助直接塞进一个被用户当成真理机器的单聊窗口里。

以前大家容忍传统搜索引擎和电商平台的流氓逻辑：
打开亚马逊搜索一个商品，第一屏密密麻麻塞了十几个竞价广告，用户虽然骂娘，但心里明镜似的知道哪条是广告、哪条是自然结果。

你骗得走我的点击，但骗不走我对界面信息的防备心，

但 AI 聊天界面的底牌完全不同，
用户不再是在成千上万个链接里做人肉筛选，而是把终极的信任和决策权，双手奉还给了屏幕上的这一行自然语言。

当一个人向 AI 询问病情、法律风险、或者给孩子选什么奶粉时，这个唯一的答案背后，哪怕只混进了一分钱的金主意志，整个信任基座瞬间就会灰飞烟灭。

最狠的是 OpenAI 这一批大模型公司现在的进退两难，
算力账单每天都在天文数字般地狂烧，光靠每个月 20 刀的订阅费根本堵不住现金流的大窟窿，引入商业广告几乎是不可避免的宿命，

但你只要敢让广告去污染生成内容的客观性，用户就会在一秒钟之内把这个曾经奉若神明的智囊，当成上门推销的廉价销售。

这里有一个极度冷酷的反直觉真相：
传统搜索卖的是展示位，AI 聊天如果卖广告，卖掉的其实是答案的灵魂。

展示位被广告塞满了还可以捏着鼻子用，
但一个一旦被怀疑收了黑钱的智能体，在用户眼里，连一句标点符号都会变成有毒的谎言。

商业化必须要做，但信任是一次性的易碎品，
未来谁能第一个在 AI 时代跑通变现，从来不看他能塞进去多少赞助商，
而看他敢不敢在商业利益把刀架在脖子上时，死死守住那条绝不篡改答案事实的红线。

text:
This article is a good step toward understanding how things really work. However, quite a few factors related to the experimental setup need to be taken into account if you want to draw more reliable conclusions:

1. The optimal shape of each architecture may differ under compute-optimal settings.
2. The optimal initialization of each parameter may differ across architectures.
3. Different architectures may respond quite differently to different optimizers.
4. Differences in training stability and the health of “internal metrics” can lead to drastically different results, even for the same architecture.
5. Architectures may respond differently to varying degrees of overtraining (tpp).
6. Different architectures may respond quite differently to different data distributions (i.e., different learning objectives).
7. The difficulty of scaling up can vary considerably across architectures.

There are many more nuances that need to be carefully addressed to obtain consistent results.

text:
Social content has obstructed art. The viewer is forced continually into a self help type state. Every video is an explanation, a lesson and show of some sort of approved social moral compass that we must all follow. There is no art. Fela Kuti took knowledge of jazz and classical music and infused it with an African drum, that was the art. His political views or social moral compass is a conversation for another time but in his creation he made art. His views did not dictate or overshadow his brilliance in art making however his creations did bring light to his perspective. Movies crafted to pull tears from one’s eyes. A beautiful art. Now content dictates how we should be feeling but not Infact making us feel. To want to create without approval of this so-called international moral facade of perfectionism feels like being painted red yet not wanting to be seen or Infact being seen. Yoko ono gave instructions, not art because art turned into a mundane practice of people coming to stare at walls. People used to go to concerts that brought them to tears, reignited something within them; made them feel. Now concerts are filled with alcohol and drugs and music that simply allows for mindless escape instead of transmutation of experience and emotion. So where are we? Who are we? What can Yoko Ono’s approach teach us today?

Be courages and go forth.

text:
raising Fund II has never been harder. only 12% of first-time VC funds from the 2022 vintage have raised a second fund so far. here are 7 reasons i think so many struggle

1. they're better at fundraising than investing

some managers are great at telling LPs what they want to hear. they have a compelling story, a convincing deck, and a thesis that sounds amazing. but can they actually pick companies that will generate returns? that's a very different skill. 50 out of 99 VC funds failed to return invested capital after fees, while 62 out of 100 failed to outperform public markets after fees and carry.

the problem is that you won't know the final results for years. by the time Fund II fundraising comes around, LPs are already judging you on early portfolio performance, the quality of your decisions, and whether your original thesis is playing out. you need to show progress before the exits happen.

2. they have no real edge in deal flow

venture returns are driven by a tiny number of exceptional companies. less than 4% of invested capital in its dataset of venture-backed exits generated returns of 10x or more. everyone wants those winners. but how are you actually going to find them and get onto their cap tables? if your strategy is just going to events, asking for intros, and competing for the same deals as everyone else, you're going to have a hard time.

you need a real reason why the best founders would come to you, ideally before everyone else knows about them. otherwise, you're often left competing for deals that stronger investors have already passed on.

3. they don't have a plan for their winners

finding a great company is only half the job. you also need enough ownership for that company to make a meaningful difference to your fund. i think this is where follow-on strategy becomes really important. as an existing investor, you get to see how founders execute, how the team works, and whether the business is actually delivering on its promises. that information can give you a real advantage when deciding where to put more capital.

of course, doubling down doesn't always make sense. valuation, dilution, and concentration risk still matter. but if you've found an exceptional company, you should have a plan for how to benefit from being right.

4. they can't explain why LPs should choose them

this one is pretty funny. VCs constantly ask founders what makes their startup different, why they'll win, and why anyone should invest. then some of those same investors go out to raise their own funds and struggle to answer exactly those questions.

what's your investor-market fit? what's your edge? why should an LP trust you instead of giving that money to an established manager? especially when you're starting out, you need a convincing answer. and the fundraising environment isn't making things easier. only 81 first-time US VC funds closed through Q3 2026.

5. they're competing in a market where capital keeps concentrating

this is probably the toughest part because even good managers can't control it. through Q3 2026, US funds of $500M+ captured 78.1% of all VC capital raised, despite representing just 6% of funds closed. firms raising their fourth fund or later took 88.2% of the capital, while the median fund size fell to $10M.

think about that. huge amounts of money are flowing into venture, but most of it is going to a relatively small group of established firms. a new manager can have a strong thesis, good founders, and a promising portfolio and still struggle to raise the next fund.

6. they underestimate how much LP relationships matter

i've seen how important this is. some managers only start building LP relationships when they're ready to raise, but by that point, they're already behind. LPs want to know how you think, how you make decisions, how you handle problems, and whether they can trust you over the long term. regular updates, honest reporting, and actually understanding what matters to each LP can make a huge difference.

ideally, by the time you start raising Fund II, your existing LPs already know exactly why they want to invest again. and if they don't, you should understand why long before fundraising starts.

7. they don't think enough about liquidity

this one is becoming increasingly important. a fund can have impressive paper returns, but LPs can't reinvest unrealized gains. TVPI matters, especially early on, but DPI tells a different story. at some point, investors want to see actual distributions. and when exits slow down, even funds with strong portfolios can struggle to return capital.

that doesn't mean every Fund I needs substantial DPI before raising Fund II. but managers should understand their portfolio's path to liquidity and be able to explain it clearly to LPs.

here are a few investors who recently raised their second funds and are worth following: @JedBreed, @jakobdiepen, @brettcalhounn, @yoheinakajima, @jamoses92, @kola_aina

text:
Hyperliquid的高估值是建立在HyperliquidL1这条专业金融链的发展壮大上（它的深度流动性让他具备做这件事的基础），而不是结算和清算的底层基础设施，因为当前最适合做底层设施的只有ETH。所以如果Hyperliquid把自己的技术模块作为基础设施去为其它交易场景服务，那么它的估值逻辑就变了。

那么Hyperliquid为什么不在L1这条路上发展壮大？我的看法是，对去中心化交易所有需求的普通用户太过于有限，当前加密市场的主要用户都在CEX，而传统金融的用户也不会离开web2的交易场景，所以去中心化交易所的客户增长瓶颈很快就会到达。因为本质上它的运营模式仍然是CEX，只是客户标签更加鲜明（.hl）。

所以我认为去中心化交易所最好的运用就是lighter这条路，站在ETH身上，去做结算和清算基础设施的运用。当然如果lighter能成为一个合规的去中心化交易所，那对用户的吸引力又不一样，因为CFTC要求必须建立符合监管要求的客户保护、风险管理和责任机制，这就解决了去中心化交易所出了事喊上帝的问题。

个人主观看法，不作为投资建议。

text:
The Binance exploiters are rushing to stay a step of stablecoin freezes. One method we’re tracking involves stashing their stablecoins in DeFi protocols. Then claiming them back on new, clean addresses.

This method has been used on the Tron blockchain since the early hours of the $6.4 billion attack. It involves swapping TRX for stablecoins, then exchanging those stablecoins for depository receipt tokens. Unlike the stablecons they represent, these receipt tokens cannot be frozen. But they can be exchanged for the stablecoins they represent by whomever holds them. That’s an edge for prospective hackers and money launderers. Especially North Korean threat actors, who have used this method on other heists, too.

Here's how North Korea's TraderTraitor group moved $500K. Step by step.

Step 1: Start with TRX. The hackers moved TRX into a swap wallet, positioning the funds for the next stage of the laundering process.

Step 2: Swap into stablecoins. The hackers converted TRX into stablecoins through a DeFi exchange. The stablecoin offers liquidity and stability, with a catch: risk of freezing. The longer you hold illicit funds in stablecoins, the more likely its centralized issuer freezes your tokens. Circle and Tether have already contributed to $2.8 billion in freezes so far. This creates a critical vulnerability for the hackers and a potential intervention point for investigators. This is a dilemma for hackers — how to exploit stablecoin liquidity without the risk of freezing.

Steps 3 and 4: Move the stablecoins: To solve the dilemma, the hackers moved the stablecoins and deposited them in a DeFi lending protocol. In return, they received a deposit token that could not be frozen. Rather than holding stablecoin directly, they now held a token representing a claim on pooled assets. They can now transfer the claim to the asset without risking a freeze. 

Steps 5 and 6: Move the claims token: The hacker moved their claim tokens to a new, clean wallet that was not tainted by association. That new wallet then converted the deposit token back to stablecoin.

Steps 7 and 8: Bridge the funds. The hackers then exfiltrated their assets from the Tron blockchain via a bridge, swapping freezable stablecoins on one side with unfreezable ETH on the other. Now the exploiter is free of worry of a freeze.

Of course, exchanging stablecoins for ETH does not make the hackers bulletproof. Chainalysis investigators analyze patterns like this to keep up with the hackers in real-time. We will continue to monitor how the blockchain is used and misused.

author: QuantusNetwork
quoted_text:
You thought this was a bad week in crypto? You might have missed the bigger news.

Two results just landed on elliptic-curve cryptography. Both are worrying. Neither one breaks a key anyone uses today.

1️⃣ The problem under ECC is less hard than we thought.

ECC is secure because the elliptic-curve discrete log is hard. The best general algorithm we had was Pollard's rho, and it is exponential: add bits to the key, and breaking it gets exponentially harder.

That assumption is now false, with one caveat. A paper from Bochum and MPI-SP gives a subexponential algorithm. It assumes an OpenAI claim that is still under review. If the claim holds, the new algorithm is faster asymptotically. In practice it changes nothing. On secp256k1, P-256, or Ed25519, rho is still the best algorithm, and it still takes the age of the universe. The new one only pulls ahead on hypothetical curves of enormous size, and there the cost is even more absurd.

https://t.co/k6ZpfloNvX

2️⃣ The quantum circuit is getting cheaper. The computer is not here.

We still have no quantum computer. The circuit that would run on one to break ECDSA keeps getting cheaper. https://t.co/bYawK8RPU3 is a public auto-research loop aimed at exactly that. Its current best is about 70% cheaper than the circuit Google reported, on logical qubits times Toffolis (0.91 billion against 2.99 billion). Google's circuit was already two to three times cheaper than the previous published one.

Alice & Bob @Alice__Bob , a French Quantum Computing company, just estimated that breaking secp256k1, the Bitcoin curve, takes at most about 30,000 cat qubits and one hour. That figure assumes a machine nobody has built. We are still far from it. The machine being asked for keeps getting smaller.

https://t.co/CXodOGwMes

What a crazy time to be alive.
