author: CryptoScoopOG
quoted_text:
The British State Is Now The Enemy Of The British People

Rupert Lowe sat down, looked into the camera, Restore lion on the frame, and said what half the country mutters in the pub and is too frightened to put on a form:

"The British state has now definitively become the enemy of the British people."

Not a critic. Not a rival. The enemy. An out-of-touch elite, addicted to central planning, treating natives like guinea pigs in a perverse experiment. An all-out war on our freedoms, escalated by an incompetent Labour government and a bloated civil service. Businesses still "private" on paper, then chained with regulation, price controls, wage diktats, employment laws, and a swarm of rapacious lawyers feeding on productive Britain like parasites.

The caption on the clip says it without apology: UK version of the USSR.

He is not wrong. He is late. And so are we.

Not the Red Flag. The Same Machine.

Nobody serious claims Britain has a Politburo and a five-year plan for tractor quotas. That is not the point. The Soviet disease was never only the hammer and sickle. It was the idea that the state owns the truth, owns the future, and owns you — and that dissent is not disagreement but pathology.

Look at Britain in 2026 and stop pretending.

Speech is policed harder than the Channel. Post the wrong flag, the wrong joke, the wrong grief about a stabbed girl, and the knock comes. Meanwhile the boats keep landing, the coaches keep waiting, and the Home Office still sells "smash the gangs" while running the reception desk. Two-tier is not a slogan invented by YouTubers. It is the lived experience of English people who get batons for a protest and soft hands for the fashionable cause.

In the USSR, the Party decided who was a good citizen. In Britain, the blob decides who is "far right." Same function. Different lanyard.

Central planning did not die in 1991. It put on a diversity badge and a net-zero spreadsheet. It tells farmers what they may grow, drivers what they may drive, parents what their children are, employers whom they must hire, and churches what they may believe. It does not need to nationalise your shop if it can regulate you into obedience and sue you into silence. Lowe's "rapacious lawyers" line is not poetry. It is the business model of a country that produces process instead of prosperity.

Guinea Pigs In The Experiment

They treated us like lab animals and called it science.

Lockdowns. Mask theatre. Mandates. The jab as morality. "Follow the science" meant follow the press release. Question it and you were dangerous. The same class that danced in empty hospitals now wants you to forget. Lowe's word was exact: guinea pigs. An elite that never shared the risk ran the trial on the nation, then promoted itself.

The experiment did not stop at COVID. It continues in the schools — sex as a feeling, boys in girls' spaces, parents as bigots for noticing biology. It continues in the councils — English flags ripped down as "hate," foreign flags flown as "culture." It continues in the hotels — military-age men from failed states housed while veterans and young couples cannot find a flat. It continues in the courts — English law for thee, parallel pressure and "community sensitivity" for the protected.

The USSR had the plan. We have the framework. Different paperwork. Same contempt for the people who pay.

Labour, The Blob, And The Lie Of Private Life

Lowe named Labour and the civil service. Good. Name them again.

Labour did not invent the betrayal. It professionalised it. Open borders as virtue. Speech law as kindness. DEI as justice. Tax as love. Every native instinct — family, border, sex reality, Christian inheritance — is treated as a hate incident waiting to happen. The Tories managed the decline and called it competence. Reform splits the right and still will not say remigration without choking. The palace stays soft where it should be steel. Traitors in suits, traitors in robes, traitors in red.

And the civil service — the permanent government — outlasts every manifesto. Bloated, insulated, addicted to process. They do not serve the British people. They serve the project: managed demographic change, managed decline of the native working class, managed guilt so you apologise for existing in your own country.

Businesses "allowed" to stay private while the state strangles them is pure late-Soviet farce. Own the means of production on the land registry; own the rules in Whitehall. Price controls here, employment law there, net-zero costs everywhere, HR departments as political commissars. Productive Britain works. Parasitic Britain litigates. Guess which one the elite prefers.

Immigration Is The Soft Occupation

You cannot talk about a British USSR and ignore the demographic weapon.

The Party imported loyalty. Our elite imports clients. Boats. Hotels. Asylum that never ends. Cities where English is optional and Sharia pressure is "community." Knife crime. Grooming. Parallel lives. Then they arrest the grandfather who says what everyone sees.

That is not diversity. That is replacement with a human-rights leaflet. Trump told Europe from Dublin that immigration is killing us. Lowe told Britain the state is the enemy. Put the two together and you get the full picture: a ruling class that will not defend the border because the border is where their project dies.

Remigration is not cruelty. It is the minimum act of a country that still wants to exist. One law. English law. No sacred carve-outs for face coverings, foreign adjudication, or identity hiring. Merit over DEI. Faces on show when order demands it. Deportation that happens, not a press release after twenty years.

Freedom Was Not Lost In One Night

The war on freedom Lowe describes was a long siege.

First they took the language — "illegal migrant" became "asylum seeker," "invasion" became "compassion," "woman" became a costume. Then they took the street — who may protest, who may film, who may gather. Then they took the child — what must be taught, what must not be questioned. Then they took the livelihood — bank, job, licence, reputation. The gulag is not always barbed wire. Sometimes it is a visit from Prevent and a ruined name.

A UK version of the USSR does not need a Berlin Wall. It needs a fearful middle class, a bought media, a weaponised police, and a public that still believes voting Labour or Tory will save them.

It will not.

The Only Way Out

Lowe is right about the diagnosis. The cure is not another Tory reboot or another Farage triangulation.

The British state must be broken of its addiction to planning our extinction. Strip the blob. End the speech police. Close the Channel as policy, not as theatre. Remigrate those who will not live as English under English law. Restore merit. Restore the family. Restore the Christian country that built the place these people are busy dismantling.

That means Restore Britain. Rupert Lowe. Not the old parties. Not the King who will not defend his own. Not Labour's traitors. Not the parasites in wigs feasting on the productive.

The British state has become the enemy of the British people.
Say it. Mean it. Vote like it is true.

Because if Lowe is right — and he is — then pretending otherwise is not moderation.
It is surrender.

The caption on the clip says it without apology: UK version of the USSR.

He is not wrong. He is late. And so are we.

Not the Red Flag. The Same Machine.

Nobody serious claims Britain has a Politburo and a five-year plan for tractor quotas. That is not the point. The Soviet disease was never only the hammer and sickle. It was the idea that the state owns the truth, owns the future, and owns you — and that dissent is not disagreement but pathology.

Look at Britain in 2026 and stop pretending.

Speech is policed harder than the Channel. Post the wrong flag, the wrong joke, the wrong grief about a stabbed girl, and the knock comes. Meanwhile the boats keep landing, the coaches keep waiting, and the Home Office still sells "smash the gangs" while running the reception desk. Two-tier is not a slogan invented by YouTubers. It is the lived experience of English people who get batons for a protest and soft hands for the fashionable cause.

In the USSR, the Party decided who was a good citizen. In Britain, the blob decides who is "far right." Same function. Different lanyard.

Central planning did not die in 1991. It put on a diversity badge and a net-zero spreadsheet. It tells farmers what they may grow, drivers what they may drive, parents what their children are, employers whom they must hire, and churches what they may believe. It does not need to nationalise your shop if it can regulate you into obedience and sue you into silence. Lowe's "rapacious lawyers" line is not poetry. It is the business model of a country that produces process instead of prosperity.

Guinea Pigs In The Experiment

They treated us like lab animals and called it science.

Lockdowns. Mask theatre. Mandates. The jab as morality. "Follow the science" meant follow the press release. Question it and you were dangerous. The same class that danced in empty hospitals now wants you to forget. Lowe's word was exact: guinea pigs. An elite that never shared the risk ran the trial on the nation, then promoted itself.

The experiment did not stop at COVID. It continues in the schools — sex as a feeling, boys in girls' spaces, parents as bigots for noticing biology. It continues in the councils — English flags ripped down as "hate," foreign flags flown as "culture." It continues in the hotels — military-age men from failed states housed while veterans and young couples cannot find a flat. It continues in the courts — English law for thee, parallel pressure and "community sensitivity" for the protected.

The USSR had the plan. We have the framework. Different paperwork. Same contempt for the people who pay.

Labour, The Blob, And The Lie Of Private Life

Lowe named Labour and the civil service. Good. Name them again.

Labour did not invent the betrayal. It professionalised it. Open borders as virtue. Speech law as kindness. DEI as justice. Tax as love. Every native instinct — family, border, sex reality, Christian inheritance — is treated as a hate incident waiting to happen. The Tories managed the decline and called it competence. Reform splits the right and still will not say remigration without choking. The palace stays soft where it should be steel. Traitors in suits, traitors in robes, traitors in red.

And the civil service — the permanent government — outlasts every manifesto. Bloated, insulated, addicted to process. They do not serve the British people. They serve the project: managed demographic change, managed decline of the native working class, managed guilt so you apologise for existing in your own country.

Businesses "allowed" to stay private while the state strangles them is pure late-Soviet farce. Own the means of production on the land registry; own the rules in Whitehall. Price controls here, employment law there, net-zero costs everywhere, HR departments as political commissars. Productive Britain works. Parasitic Britain litigates. Guess which one the elite prefers.

Immigration Is The Soft Occupation

You cannot talk about a British USSR and ignore the demographic weapon.

The Party imported loyalty. Our elite imports clients. Boats. Hotels. Asylum that never ends. Cities where English is optional and Sharia pressure is "community." Knife crime. Grooming. Parallel lives. Then they arrest the grandfather who says what everyone sees.

That is not diversity. That is replacement with a human-rights leaflet. Trump told Europe from Dublin that immigration is killing us. Lowe told Britain the state is the enemy. Put the two together and you get the full picture: a ruling class that will not defend the border because the border is where their project dies.

Remigration is not cruelty. It is the minimum act of a country that still wants to exist. One law. English law. No sacred carve-outs for face coverings, foreign adjudication, or identity hiring. Merit over DEI. Faces on show when order demands it. Deportation that happens, not a press release after twenty years.

Freedom Was Not Lost In One Night

The war on freedom Lowe describes was a long siege.

First they took the language — "illegal migrant" became "asylum seeker," "invasion" became "compassion," "woman" became a costume. Then they took the street — who may protest, who may film, who may gather. Then they took the child — what must be taught, what must not be questioned. Then they took the livelihood — bank, job, licence, reputation. The gulag is not always barbed wire. Sometimes it is a visit from Prevent and a ruined name.

A UK version of the USSR does not need a Berlin Wall. It needs a fearful middle class, a bought media, a weaponised police, and a public that still believes voting Labour or Tory will save them.

It will not.

The Only Way Out

Lowe is right about the diagnosis. The cure is not another Tory reboot or another Farage triangulation.

The British state must be broken of its addiction to planning our extinction. Strip the blob. End the speech police. Close the Channel as policy, not as theatre. Remigrate those who will not live as English under English law. Restore merit. Restore the family. Restore the Christian country that built the place these people are busy dismantling.

That means Restore Britain. Rupert Lowe. Not the old parties. Not the King who will not defend his own. Not Labour's traitors. Not the parasites in wigs feasting on the productive.

The British state has become the enemy of the British people.
Say it. Mean it. Vote like it is true.

Because if Lowe is right — and he is — then pretending otherwise is not moderation.
It is surrender.

text:
Hedge funds just hit the panic button harder than at any time in the last ten years. Here is why that is good news for you.

Morgan Stanley tracks the total money its hedge fund clients have bet on stocks. When that total drops sharply, it means funds are being forced to cut positions, usually because their losses hit a limit. In the last 2 days, it fell 7.8%, a bigger unwind than the Covid crash, the GameStop squeeze, or the 2016 and 2018 selloffs.

Every time this number fell past 6% (2016, 2018 twice, 2020, 2021, 2025), the S&P 500 bottomed within a week or two and was higher one, three and six months later. Six out of six.

The reason is simple. Once the forced sellers have sold, there is nobody left to push prices down. Those same funds then have to buy back in, and that buying has powered every rebound in the table.

As for me, I am looking for great businesses that got dumped for no reason. That is where the bargains are.

quoted_text:
NOVA: Emission Split Update for Data Generation Fund
Owner 26% / Miners 33% / Validators 41%

With the launch of eTAO, subnet owners can now adjust how emissions are distributed. NOVA will be updating its split to allocate more resources toward what we believe is the highest-impact investment we can make in the subnet's future: experimental data generation.

Wet lab data is the best investment we can make both to prove out what the subnet produces and to increase the value of what gets built on top of it.

Data is the bottleneck
AI-driven drug discovery faces a fundamental constraint: the quality of our predictions is ultimately limited by the experimental data available to train and validate them.

Much of today's publicly available drug discovery data is fragmented across studies, generated using different experimental protocols, and inconsistent in quality and coverage.

Generating high-quality experimental data allows us to address that limitation directly. It gives miners better ground truth for model development, provides independent validation of their predictions, and helps us identify which approaches actually translate into experimental success.

The industry is making the same bet.

Some of the largest investments in AI-driven biology are now directed toward generating the experimental data necessary to train and validate better models.

Biohub committed $400M of a $500M, five-year initiative to data generation, infrastructure and measurement technology, and later expanded into a $1.8B effort backed by Meta, Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs, who collectively committed $300M.

The OpenAI Foundation gave $15M to OpenADMET to generate public ADME datasets, which will be used in prospective blind challenges against newly measured experimental data. Octant continues the high-throughput data generation behind it. 

Leash Bio used a $9.3M seed round to scale data collection for a foundational medicinal chemistry model, producing a dataset that screened 133 million molecules against each protein. 

Anthropic has set up a physical biology lab in the Bay Area.

What the additional funds will support
The additional owner allocation will go into a dedicated R&D fund for wet lab data generation.

1. ADME model training competition. The first use of the fund is generating the experimental data behind our ADME competition, currently in design and development. High-quality, standardized ADME data is what turns a competition from a benchmark into something that produces models with real predictive value.

2. Advancing assets under development. Where it makes sense, the fund can also support experimental work that moves our in-development assets forward.

Why this benefits the entire NOVA ecosystem
We believe generating experimental data is one of the most effective ways to increase the long-term value of the subnet.

For miners, better datasets and scientifically grounded evaluations create opportunities to develop more capable models, compete on meaningful performance improvements, and contribute work with greater real-world utility.

For validators, stronger experimental benchmarks improve the ability to assess model quality and reward useful contributions.

For tokenholders, better models, experimentally validated discoveries, and progress toward valuable therapeutic assets can strengthen NOVA's competitive position and long-term commercial potential.

The economic opportunity extends beyond any individual competition. We are building an increasingly capable scientific discovery platform, and the data generated through our R&D efforts can become a compounding asset for the entire ecosystem.

Miner incentives remain strong
Miners will still receive a meaningfully larger share than the owner (33% vs. 26%), and we believe the rewards will preserve healthy, competitive incentives for participation. Better data and better-validated competitions also make the work miners do more valuable over time.

Protecting token health
Funds from the R&D allocation will be converted to cover lab costs gradually, distributed over time rather than sold in size, to limit market impact and preserve token health.

The bottom line
We think this is the single best thing we can do to accelerate our progress, increase our chance of success, and create value for everyone with a stake in NOVA, including miners, validators, and tokenholders. It is time for us to scale real-world validation.

最狠的是他把这套方法，直接对标到了 SpaceX 当年那个近乎自杀的疯狂决定上。

猎鹰 9 号明明是全人类商业航天史上最赚钱、发射成功率最高的王牌火箭，现金流好到可以躺着吃二十年；

但马斯克反手就要把它彻底淘汰，把全部身家性命押注在连炸了几次的 Starship 星舰上。

这就像当年科尔特斯率军登陆后亲手烧掉退路的战船一样，不给自己留一丝苟活的余地。

Sellis 感叹说，全世界几乎没有哪家大公司能做到 SpaceX 这种程度。

因为人性骨子里都在恋战舒适区，宁愿在一条注定沉没的大船上数钞票，也不愿意跳进冰水里去造下一艘核潜艇。

其实这里有一个极度冷酷的反直觉真相：
商业世界最危险的状态，从来不是你面临绝境，而是你手里正捧着一只利润丰厚的金饭碗。

敢亲手砸碎自己最赚钱的现金牛，
往往是在未来大浪打过来时，唯一能保住整条命的活路。
author: AYi_AInotes
quoted_text:
英伟达CEO兼创始人黄仁勋在CNN专访里公开了自己的一个极度反直觉的日常习惯：
他每天都在疯狂用 AI，但他觉得自己的大脑反而越来越聪明了。

很多人用 AI 的方式，本质上是在给自己搞脑力大截肢，
比如写个邮件让它润色，写个总结让它代笔，遇到一点需要动脑的死结，顺手就把键盘推给模型让它替自己下决定。

把工具当成偷懒的拐杖，结果用了半年，手艺全废了，自己彻底退化成了离了对话框就不会思考的巨婴。

但老黄在访谈里直接撕开了这层遮羞布，
他说他从来不让 AI 替自己思考，
他是让 AI 当自己的私教，
去教自己完全不懂的全新领域，
或者去啃那些靠肉身经验根本啃不动的硬骨头。

不要拿它去做你本来就能做的事，而是拿它去推开你原本根本跨不过去的认知高墙。

最狠的是扎卡利亚追问时，黄仁勋提到的那个做 CEO 的真实底牌。

他说作为掌管几万亿美元芯片帝国的掌门人，他每天 90% 的指令，本质上都不是在下命令，而是在疯狂向团队、向模型提出高质量的问题。

给大模型写提示词，从来不是什么输入几个关键词的机械杂活，提问本身就是一项极度消耗脑力的顶级认知技能。

这里有一个残酷的反直觉真相：
AI 正在以光速拉开两类人的贫富差距。

一类人把思考外包给机器，每天省下半小时摸鱼，认知全面萎缩，

另一类人把执行外包给机器，逼着自己去深挖真问题，每天借着全球顶级的算力给自己完成一次大脑重塑。

所以咱们别再问 AI 会不会让人变笨了，工具没有任何道德偏好，
你把它当轮椅，你就会变成瘫子，你把它当杠杆，你就能一个人撬动一整个智囊团。

X刚推出的新订阅模式The X Subscription！将蓝V、Grok、Grok Bot 以及Cursor等权益被整合进同一套订阅生态，用户不再需要为了不同功能反复折腾。

再加上支付宝支付入口的打通，原本复杂的订阅流程一下子简单了许多。一次订阅，多个权益，支付门槛也降低了。不是单纯卖一个蓝V，而是借助 X 的庞大用户基础，把社交、AI 和付费订阅整合到一起。

不得不说，老马是真的懂互联网用户。A畜和Chatgpt还在关注 AI 模型之间的竞争时，都忽略了一个非常现实的问题：你产品再强，用户连钱都付不了，又怎么抢占市场？

过去，中国用户想体验海外 AI 产品，第一步不是研究模型有多厉害，而是先去研究海外信用卡、虚拟卡和各种代充渠道。

技术决定产品的上限，支付决定用户增长的下限。

text:
AI has BROKEN the internet's traditional traffic model.

Reddit’s earnings call yesterday offers a stark example. 

CEO Steve Huffman said: “AI mode does not drive traffic. Not for us and not to anybody as far as I know.”

Search referrals to Reddit fell by more than 1 MILLION per week on average in October. 

$RDDT shares plunged around 25% on Friday as traffic concerns and a weaker outlook overshadowed its earnings.

For decades, the arrangement was straightforward where websites created content, search engines sent them visitors, and those visits generated advertising revenue, subscriptions and sales.

AI has changed that exchange - 

A search engine can now summarize a website’s information and answer follow-up questions without the reader ever visiting the source.

The content still helps answer the question but the website may never get the click.

Pew’s March 2025 study found users clicked traditional search results on 8% of visits with AI summaries, compared with 15% without them. 

That's nearly a -50% drawdown in clicks.

Google faces its own transition. Alphabet fell 12.6% on Thursday after slower Search growth and heavy AI spending cloud investors’ concerns. 

Its search business is still growing, but monetization has not caught up with the changing usage.

More questions can now be answered while fewer visitors reach the websites supplying the information.

That leaves publishers facing a fundamental challenge in finding a way to earn from content that remains useful even when the audience never arrives.

text:
Leaving Lisbon today with a lot to think about after my first Meridian.

One thing I keep coming back to is how much of building an ecosystem happens after the events are over. Getting people into a room is one thing. Helping them stick around, keep building, and turn an idea into something people actually use is another.

3 things I’m taking away from Meridian:

1. Retention over acquisition, again and again.

getting developers into the ecosystem is just the beginning. The real challenge is helping them stay, build long-term, and turn their projects into startups.

2. Traction over demos.

a good demo is a starting point. I plan to focus more on understanding what’s blocking teams, helping them find their first users, and supporting them as they scale.

3. More collaboration across chapters.

meeting all the Stellar Chapter Leads and Ambassadors was amazing. Now it’s time to turn those connections into more cross-chapter collaborations and opportunities for our builders.

Hope to see you all again very soon 💛

the binance hacker dumped $200m of altcoins: uni, ena, pepe, link, aave, ondo, wld. he got $158m for them.

the problem: binance has to buy every single one back. its proof of reserves depends on it.

and it’s doing it. binance says it’s buying them on market and otc. overnight, 128.6m ena (~$24m) went in a binance wallet.

the hacker sold 13–28% below pre-hack prices. 21% on average.

since then, those coins bounced 13–36% from his sale prices.

buying back the same bag today costs ~$192m.
that’s $33m more than the hacker ever got.

the winners is whoever bought this dump, knowing binance will be forced to buyback.

quoted_text:
昨晚跟168X的交流要点，上一次8月底https://t.co/MrasWYxXvC参与168X聊到：美股临近中期选举市场动荡加大，然后大饼和加密到10月因为流动性收紧会回踩。梳理下这次聊的要点：
1、美国经济正在进入由AI基建驱动的新基建周期，这种大基建趋势下名义GDP的增速会很好；

2、中东局势中期选举后可能会是一个时间窗口，如果能解决油价回落宏观环境压力会减少很多；
但如果一直不能解决油价持续在高位，通胀持续强势那么联储不仅12月会加息，明年也可能会加，如果原来预期 2 次，最后变成 3 次、4 次甚至更久，则整个估值体系都会重新定价、市场会扛不住。

3、ARR这个指标需要抛后，Anthropic上市后就要看真实的季度营收、年度营收了。大云平台已经是AI Operating System：企业会从结果和成本考虑，切换不同的模型。

4、大型科技公司真正大规模提高 CapEx，是从 2025 年三季度左右开始的，所以今天 Microsoft、Google Cloud 增长出来的 Revenue，很多对应的其实是一年前甚至更早花出去的钱。去年下半年开始加速建设的 Capacity，现在才进入投产期，而过去几个季度所有云厂商一直在讲同一句话：Demand > Supply，算力不够。如果需求还在增长，而且你新上线多少 Capacity 都能马上被吃掉，那未来几个季度 Revenue 自然会继续加速。所以我觉得AI商业化现在不是见顶，而是才刚开始加速。

5、要看Cloud Revenue Growth 何时开始超过 CapEx Growth
不能永远只看 Revenue，第二阶段要看 ROIC。2026 年是 CapEx 爆发的一年。去年几千亿美元，今年接近翻倍，这种 CapEx Growth 不可能每年都 100%。
真正漂亮的拐点是什么？就是未来 CapEx Growth 开始自然下降，但 AI Revenue Growth 还继续加速、意味着开始算的过账来。

所以接下来几个季度，最想看的就是：Revenue Growth、CapEx Growth、Depreciation Life、FCF，这几个东西开始怎么收敛。

6、AI主线已经迁移：Memory → Optical / Software → Agent / AI for Science/应用

不要形成“AI = Semiconductor = Memory”的定式思维，一说AI就是半导体、一说半导体就是存储。

每一阶段 AI 的主线都会迁移。今年一季度、二季度，Memory 是最强的；到 8、9 月以后，Optical 开始变强，同时一批之前被砸得很惨的软件、SaaS 也开始走出来。为什么？因为模型商品化、Token Price 下来以后，受益的不只上游 硬件。Token 越便宜，Deployment 越容易，Cloud、Software、Enterprise Integration、Agent 反而会越来越受益。再下一阶段可能就是 AI for Science、Bio、更广泛的应用层。

所以趋势投资真正要做的，不是死守原来的 Winner，而是不断识别：下一层利润池正在往哪里迁移。Semi 也不是死了，只是像上半年那种所有东西直线上冲的阶段，短期可能过去了。

7、真正需要让 AI Thesis 转空的信号，不是 Semi 再跌 20%，而是 AI商业化（云厂商业绩增速）开始降速、当下是出于加速的阶段。这才是未来的市场的真正的大风险，

而另一个问题则是伊朗问题迟迟得不到解决，油价高位、通胀向上趋势被强化、联储不得不多次加息而非两次。

8、高收益率时代不再普涨：以后市场只奖励真实 Cash Flow。
当 Bond Yield 高以后，股票自然也要给更高的 Risk Premium，这就是为什么现在市场越来越挑剔。Google Cloud很好，Search、FCF 出现问题，市场照样先卖。所以之后选股票一定要分清楚：哪些公司只是 Narrative，哪些公司的业务已经真正兑现，Revenue 是真的、Cash Flow 是真的，而且未来 2、3 年增长空间还能算出来。

大公司如果因为短期逆风被杀估值，我反而觉得是好事，因为它给你重新上车的价格。高利率不是所有股票不能涨，而是市场会越来越“优中选优”。

9、中期选举后很多不确定性会减弱如国会的归属，再看伊朗问题是不是能解决，谨防Anthropic上市路演开始后的吸血。

昨天有一点现在看是不对的“昨天聊到如果亚马逊的财报还不错、市场有一波能到anthropic路演前、今年亚马逊财报云业务很好但是广告放缓、资本开支远超预期、也是加重了市场担忧”可能这种担忧要到中期选举之后再看了。

多谢@168MrZ

quoted_text:
Later today, we are officially ending all remaining support for the Iron Fish network.

A few days ago, we observed abnormal activity involving wIRON and the ChainPort bridge. After working with ChainPort and reviewing their logs, we discovered that the cause was an inflation bug in the Iron Fish blockchain itself.

We traced the bug to a commit from early 2019 in the Merkle tree implementation. The developer at the time implemented a standard Merkle tree. However, because of nuances in how a note’s nullifier is calculated (the mechanism that lets a normal user spend their funds), the attacker was able to spend the same note more than once. 

The attacker then compounded the exploit, aggregated their notes, and exited through the ChainPort bridge. This code path was within the scope of both our external and internal audits, but the bug wasn’t caught during review.

For closure, we’ve committed the patch for the exploit, with a detailed postmortem included in the PR, before shutting down and archiving the ironfish repo.

The meta-analysis here is that software that can’t be upgraded immediately (most of crypto), is in an extremely precarious position. The ability to find and exploit vulnerabilities in technically complex code is becoming commoditized. Safety guardrails on US frontier models make it difficult for companies to use them to patch security vulnerabilities, while abliterated open-source models are approaching frontier capabilities.

We wish everyone all the best, and we hope crypto finds a path through this. 

Thank you all.

text:
⚖️ The Future Is Tradable: six talks on prediction markets, AI agents and who decides what happened, from the Kleros × @seer_pm evening at @4seasDeSoc in Chiang Mai.

Each speaker took one question.

Are prediction markets informative yet? @clesaege showed that trading volume is there, but most of it is sports and parlays, and very little of it produces information anyone can use.

Who predicts people best? @devanshmehta taught the basic market types and shared a finding from the Deep Funding work: old market data fit new human judgments better than the old human data did.

Can an agent trade for you? @MPouramiri built a reusable AI skill that researches a market, writes its own estimate, sizes the position and queues the trade only if the edge survives.

Who decides what happened? @JuanRah covered resolution: a market needs an answer people accept, that arrives by a deadline and holds up with money on the line.

How do you pay for an answer? @distbit0 presented answer markets, where contributors are paid by how much they change an LLM judge's mind.

Who sets the goals? @clesaege closed with AI agents trading on information finance: pay machines to be right, and let people set the goals.

Thanks to @weiwei_ooi for organizing the night and to everyone who came to trade.

All six talks are on YouTube. Links in the replies.

quoted_text:
Saw a few discussions about size of hack, why impact to bitcoin price is small, etc. 👇 

$6.3 billion is the biggest in USD terms, but not in BTC terms. MtGox was 650,000 BTC!

Other important numbers to consider:

% of bitcoin (in relation to BTC total supply), ie, market impact. MtGox is big there again at 5%+.

Number of users impacted, and % of user assets impacted. MtGox (the largest CEX at the time) and FTX (not small) were all near 100% of users and their asseets.

Most important: Who is impacted? Does the platform cover it all? (only one victim), as in recent two CEX cases and Binance.

Obviously, still a major disaster for the industry, Binance (and me). It hurts, but we survive. 

Most importantly, we protect our users.

(image from @MatthewRoszak)

I lead product for Claude subscriptions. Today we're renaming our Max plans, and I want to explain why.

When we launched our top plan in April 2025, it had a single limit: 5 hours. It gave you 20x Pro's limit, so we called it Max 20x. When we added weekly limits to Max 20x, we set them to 10x Pro's (the 5-hour limit stayed at 20x).

I get that some new users assumed 20x applied to both limits. We could have done better here, and I'm sorry.

The Ultra plan keeps the weekly limit (10x Pro), but we're removing the 5-hour limit so you can keep building without getting blocked mid-session. This starts today and rolls out in stages. To help prevent fraud and abuse, a temporary limit applies until we've verified your account. You'll get an email when your limit is removed.

We've got more cooking and can't wait to share it. Thanks for building with Claude 🙏

text:
This isn’t a coincidence. Europe is beginning to coalesce around a scheme to tax foreign AI firms in an effort to recoup a fiscal shortfall brought on by AI. It probably won’t work, but it makes sense: 

- AI tilts the factor share of income away from labor towards capital. Not the whole way, it’s just not 70/30 any more (70 being labor). Maybe it’s 60/40. This should be obvious. This doesn’t mean output falls. Probably output and productivity rise, it’s just that capital captures a larger share. 

- this fundamentally challenges the way developed states collect tax which is mainly on labor and wages. European nations in particular rely on personal income, payroll taxes and social contributions to fund grossly engorged welfare states. States must make up the lost payroll taxes by capturing the gains accruing to capital. But wait! Capital is a foreign AI firm. The AI firm disrupting domestic labor is probably not domestic in origin (for Europe). So there’s nothing left to tax. 

- European nations are mainly consumers rather than producers of AI. A producer nation has a similar problem - it must tax capital more aggressively to make up for lost labor income, but this is tractable - but a consumer nation has a much worse problem. Europe will face the substitution of domestic labor for foreign inference which benefits the owners of a largely foreign AI supply chain. When a French professional services firm gets disrupted and loses 70% of its staff due to AI productivity gain, the French government can’t tax Anthropic over in California to make up for the lost payroll and personal income taxes. The laid off French workers will also spend less reducing consumption tax receipts domestically. 

Some savings will remain in France as consumer surplus via lower prices but that’s not easily taxable. The French firm itself might be more profitable after it replaces staff with AI, and that is captured but that doesn’t make up the shortfall. 

- Europe has a few options. They will attempt all of them. They can a) regulate away AI disruption by banning AI use in professional fields. They can b) try and capture the tilt towards capital by fostering their own domestic industry of AI firms. They can c) try and extract rents from the foreign AI firms that are disrupting them. 

A) is the obvious move, make it illegal for an AI model to provide medical, legal, or accounting advice (etc). This will be very unpopular in the end but it will definitely be attempted. This is already underway. It will make these countries less productive and less competitive in the global market. And it wont work. People will find ways to use frontier AI. Diffusion will be slower but not inhibited. This will worsen Europe's fiscal situation overall by making it a worse place to do business and putting a drag on growth.

B) is another obvious move – if Anthropic is disrupting French white collar labor, ban Anthropic and support a domestic competitor - the Le Gros Chaton model or whatever. The only problem is that Europe appears incapable of creating a frontier model. They have the talent but not the right regulatory model or incentive to form capital locally. AI could have been invented in Europe, and many of its component parts and researchers are European, but the winning AI firms were largely not capitalized there, because of the exact thing we're talking about - an engorged welfare state and a high tax burden required to support it. Also, Europe has engaged in suicidal deindustrialization so it isn't competitive when it comes to the more fundamental inputs to AI like power and data centers. Thus, Europe will mainly be an importer and consumer of inference rather than a seller. Structurally, Europe will not be able to marshal capital locally which it could then shift the fiscal burden onto. European firms will continue to consume foreign inference. 

C) is where we land, and this explains Europe's behavior with these new exotic taxes on internet use and AI. Europe will have to contrive a way to try and recoup lost labor taxes by taxing foreign capital. American tech companies tolerate this for now as a nuisance cost of doing business in Europe, but this will eventually reach a fever pitch as Europe continues to raise the stakes. Want access to the European market? Pay us $10b/year in "fines" (taxes). Now pay us $100b a year. At some point, Europe will exhaust American tech companies' ability to pay and they will exit the market. Moreover, this is only a partial measure and depends on a benevolent America tolerating ankle-biting without taking punitive measures. The US has already begun applying pressure to Europe to stop coattail-riding via NATO and this will only accelerate, so Europe will have a very limited ability to extract fines. This won't work in the end, but expect to hear a lot about it in the coming years. 

In the end, Europe will benefit from AI as productivity gains diffuse throughout society, but AI will further deteriorate its already tenuous fiscal situation. Europe cannot cope with a situation in which domestic labor is outsourced to foreign inference, and it has an extremely limited ability to deal with this. I don't expect total collapse, but a continued erosion in standards of living and relevance, especially if they don't make the hard choices of slashing immigration, massive welfare states, and spending on the elderly.

People should pay attention to DeWEB (@Blonskr @TapeOutWorld) for web app security in the AI era.

Just a few hours ago, @blockaid_ flagged 12 crypto sites serving a wallet drainer, and @flapdotsh  and @Kintsu confirmed DNS hijacks. Right URL, attacker's code, no contract bug needed.

@VitalikButerin is experimenting with digital minimalism. One part is web minimalism, relying less on website UIs. One reason, you re-download a web application from the server on every visit, so if the server gets hacked even once, you might be screwed. 

Towards the issue, vitalik's answer is CLI tools and local AI. DeWeb tackles the same risk differently. For DeWeb, website lives on blockchain. You download website from  blockchain through multiple RPCs, and reject any mismatch. With a local client, there's no server or domain to hijack. 

The attack shifts to the owner's private key for modifying on chain website content, where every change is public on chain, or to several RPCs lying in sync.

纽交所母公司 ICE 删帖又重发，https://t.co/EMdUCKN9eM 合作并未取消，但这次明显多了监管前提。

ICE 最新公告确认，计划将 https://t.co/EMdUCKN9eM 基于 Hyperliquid 的永续合约引入美国市场，覆盖加密资产、股票、指数、大宗商品和外汇。

但与此前公告相比，新增了两个关键限定：「计划引入」和「须经监管批准」。

如果获批，ICE 将负责运营 https://t.co/EMdUCKN9eM 的美国受监管版本，用户通过美国监管的期货佣金商（FCM）访问平台，并接受 KYC/AML 审核。新交易场所将独立于 ICE 现有机构期货业务。

这意味着 ICE 并非简单地把 Hyperliquid 搬进美国，而是希望借助自身监管体系和 https://t.co/EMdUCKN9eM 的技术经验，将链上永续合约接入美国合规交易市场。

此前 ICE 删除原帖，一度引发市场对合作取消的猜测。如今重新发布并补充监管条件，更像是法务团队对公告措辞进行了谨慎调整。

真正值得关注的是：如果这项计划最终落地，Hyperliquid 的技术与流动性生态，或将通过 ICE 这样的传统金融基础设施进入美国市场。

David Friedberg says every dollar Nvidia spends making chips turns into $18 of Anthropic revenue, with SpaceX making an 83% margin in between

“I basically said start with NVIDIA, how much does NVIDIA spend to make the chips? And then how much do they sell the chips for? So for every dollar of COGS, every dollar that NVIDIA spends, that turns into $4 of revenue for NVIDIA, 75% margin."

"And then that gets sold to SpaceX, and then SpaceX turns around, and they’re making, you know, an 83% margin on that chip spend, because they’re kind of looking at a five-year depreciation. So they spent $10 billion on Colossus one, five year life, $2 billion a year depreciation. And so that’s kind of the cost per year, but then they’re making $1.25 billion a month on Colossus."

"And then Anthropic is showing in this S-1 pretty remarkably to Sacks’s point that they’re making about 85% incremental gross margin on every incremental dollar coming in. It’s obviously a baseline of compute spend, but 85% is kind of the incremental gross margin. So at the end of the day, a dollar that NVIDIA spends turns into $18 that Anthropic is making selling to customers.”

text:
Preference Model（Anthropic系创始人） 是一家总部位于旧金山的「超级智能数据研究公司」，专注于为前沿 AI 实验室构建强化学习（RL）环境，用于训练更强能力、更好对齐的模型。⁠

公司的核心观点：模型的行为几乎完全由训练时的奖励信号塑造。因此，他们专注于构建高质量、抗「奖励黑客」（reward hacking）的 RL 环境，把训练 harness 和评分器（graders）当作攻击面来加固，防止模型找到捷径或漏洞来获取高分，而不是真正解决问题。

过去一年，公司已为多家前沿实验室构建 RL 环境，尤其聚焦 ML 研究与工程任务（如写 CUDA kernel、数据策展、实验设计等），因为这是当前实验室最看重的能力提升方向。

核心开源项目：Karotte（之前介绍过该项目）：
-提供RL 环境构建框架。
-提供安全默认设置与原语，主动防御常见奖励黑客手段（沙箱隔离、非特权运行、评分前杀掉残留进程、拒绝危险文件、防止 OOM/fork bomb 等）。
-已在内部经过超过 100 万次评估运行和对抗性红队测试，用于生产环境。

团队：
Jennifer Zhou：联合创始人兼 CEO。曾在 Anthropic 数据团队早期工作，负责构建预训练数据基础设施、tokenizer 以及 Claude 的预训练数据集；

融资：
2026 年 10 月 7 日宣布完成 1600 万美元种子轮，由 a16z 领投。天使投资人包括 Fei-Fei Li、Ian Goodfellow、Julian Schrittwieser 等知名研究者等。

币安被盗后，黑客急着把稳定币换成 ETH，却在短时间内推高了链上交易价格。一场套利争夺随之展开，也让一家只有 16 人的公司登上了 DefiLlama 协议收入榜首。

黑客换币造成价差后，套利机器人争相交易。为了让交易更快、更靠前地上链，它们向区块构建者支付了高额费用。据 Bitquery 统计，当晚机器人支付的小费达到 10,251 枚 ETH，前一晚同一时段只有 4.6 枚。

Titan 的位置也由此受到关注：它构建了以太坊约一半的区块，旗下中继连接了超过 90% 的验证者。今年 3 月，一笔交易因滑点设置错误，也曾让 Titan 单日收入冲上榜首。

一家十几人的公司，如何在三年里拿下近半数以太坊区块的构建份额？黑客换币产生的价差，最终又流向了谁？

text:
看完今天两个小时的台北市长辩论，我整体感觉是平分秋色。但如果非要分个高下，蒋万安的「预期管理」做得非常好。本来我觉得他及格就好，结果表现和气势都判若两人，甚至让都怀疑是早就布局好的。

蒋万安和他的团队前期选战非常低调，可以说是被压着打，很被动。但他们选择不怎么摆政绩，等沈伯洋先把架势摆开，再去找他选举布局里的漏洞。

今天的交叉质询，有点像现任市长拿自己对市政的熟悉度来考沈伯洋，细到：大同斯文里都更为什么卡了十年，0到6岁每周免费临托4小时要多少保姆，市民大道「缝合」到底缝什么。政绩留到申论一口气讲完：「四年前我说到，四年后我做到。」如果这真是事先想好的，说明蒋和他的幕僚是有水平的。

对沈伯洋来说比较难受的是，他其实很难反驳蒋万安的主要政见。大巨蛋、辉达、免费营养午餐，台北市民大多是认的。所以沈伯洋自己也说：「没有人在否定免费的营养午餐」（但台北也不是第一个推营养午餐的县市），问题出在执行。这就是为什么他有一个问题一直在追问 SOP：东门茄苳树为什么会被误砍，不出席会议的标准是什么。蒋万安一直绕开，直到结论只能补一句，说是厂商没按要求移植，已经严惩。

另外说说我自己的想法。我从小在大陆受教育，知道体制内对「优秀政治人物」的标准不太一样：喜怒不形于色，多讲官话，不暴露真实想法，没有真心就没有破绽。蒋万安给我的感觉也是这样，国民党不少老一辈政治人物都是这个风格。之前上政论节目，几个主持人问人事问题问到急了，说他没魄力，他照样不接。今天沈伯洋问他为什么不出席会议，他也只回开了很多专案会议，市府就是「分层负责，抓大方向」。

沈伯洋更像大学教授，靠真诚打动人。他会讲自己当年列表格比较美国和台湾，为了打开青少年的心房去学塔罗牌，遇到自由潜水场馆这种问题答不上来，就回去做功课。这种人在一人一分钟的交叉质询里很吃亏，他自己都抱怨「我们来回只能问四个问题」，最后还问蒋万安要不要再约一场，加 LINE 也行。所以我有个反常识的看法：沈伯洋更适合王伟忠、赵少康那种一对一的长访谈，时间够长，真诚才能打动人。

最后借蔡康永前几天在节目上说的一句话：
“不用管哪个候选人会赢，把票投给你想要的生活方式，你就赢了。” 他现在蓝绿两边的造势场子都去过，沈伯洋今天在结论里也念了这句。

text:
X 产品负责人Peter不愧是目前世界上对顶级的产品经理，永远可以相信马斯克选人的眼光，
在这段 1分多钟的访谈里，Peter把所有大模型公司最痛但又最不敢公开说的大实话捅穿了：

在 AI 聊天产品里插广告完全行得通，但它随时会直接杀死这家公司的整条命。

要知道这不是又一次在页面边栏挂个横幅广告，也不是在信息流里那种划过去就算了的赞助推文，

这是人类互联网历史上，第一次把商业赞助直接塞进一个被用户当成真理机器的单聊窗口里。

以前大家容忍传统搜索引擎和电商平台的流氓逻辑：
打开亚马逊搜索一个商品，第一屏密密麻麻塞了十几个竞价广告，用户虽然骂娘，但心里明镜似的知道哪条是广告、哪条是自然结果。

你骗得走我的点击，但骗不走我对界面信息的防备心，

但 AI 聊天界面的底牌完全不同，
用户不再是在成千上万个链接里做人肉筛选，而是把终极的信任和决策权，双手奉还给了屏幕上的这一行自然语言。

当一个人向 AI 询问病情、法律风险、或者给孩子选什么奶粉时，这个唯一的答案背后，哪怕只混进了一分钱的金主意志，整个信任基座瞬间就会灰飞烟灭。

最狠的是 OpenAI 这一批大模型公司现在的进退两难，
算力账单每天都在天文数字般地狂烧，光靠每个月 20 刀的订阅费根本堵不住现金流的大窟窿，引入商业广告几乎是不可避免的宿命，

但你只要敢让广告去污染生成内容的客观性，用户就会在一秒钟之内把这个曾经奉若神明的智囊，当成上门推销的廉价销售。

这里有一个极度冷酷的反直觉真相：
传统搜索卖的是展示位，AI 聊天如果卖广告，卖掉的其实是答案的灵魂。

展示位被广告塞满了还可以捏着鼻子用，
但一个一旦被怀疑收了黑钱的智能体，在用户眼里，连一句标点符号都会变成有毒的谎言。

商业化必须要做，但信任是一次性的易碎品，
未来谁能第一个在 AI 时代跑通变现，从来不看他能塞进去多少赞助商，
而看他敢不敢在商业利益把刀架在脖子上时，死死守住那条绝不篡改答案事实的红线。
author: AYi_AInotes
quoted_text:
黄仁勋在 CNN 专访里公开了一个让所有硅谷高管心惊肉跳的管理细节：

英伟达内部 100% 的软件工程师和芯片设计师已经在天天用 AI，他推行的力度甚至到了“近乎强制”的地步。

而且不是那种流于形式的发发倡议、也不是HR安排的打卡培训，

老黄就是把这件事情当成了公司生死存亡的红线：

只要你在英伟达写代码、画芯片图纸，你就必须把一部分脑力外包给大模型。

以前很多大厂程序员总有一种老手艺人的傲慢：
觉得 AI 生成的代码太脏，逻辑有漏洞，只有人肉一行一行敲出来的才叫工程素养。

换个工具就等于全盘否定自己过去十几年的肌肉记忆，甚至暗搓搓地抗拒把业务细节喂给模型。

但黄仁勋这一巴掌把这种矫情彻底拍碎了，
哪怕在英伟达这个造芯片、卖算力的大本营里，连最硬核的一线工程师都被 CEO 按着头全面接入 AI，

黄仁勋自己手机里更是常年挂着四个工具：ChatGPT、Gemini Pro、Perplexity 和 Grok 轮番换着用。

现在当卖铲子的人都在把铲子硬塞进自己人的喉咙里，外面的观望者还在争论要不要用，本身就是一种极其荒诞的代际时差。

我觉得最狠的是扎卡利亚追问的那句“英语专业的复仇”，

以前进入计算机世界的门票，被 C++、Python、Verilog 这些晦涩的机器语法死死垄断，

但现在的计算机在疯狂适配人类的母语，未来唯一的编程语言就是英语，就是你说的人话。

text:
Many of you are in the process of applying for jobs in academia and/or in industry. 

As you prepare your job talks, consider giving it the following structure: 

First, a short snippet of your overall set of technical accomplishments. For instance, you might spend the first 15 minutes giving short overviews of a few of your works/papers - it's also very good to draw a theme across them if there is one.

Second, you can spend the next 20-25 minutes doing a deep dive on *just one* of them - say, the one you're most proud of, or the one that matches the team/department interests and needs best.

Finally, use the last 5-10 minutes to summarize and talk about what you think are important new directions to pursue in research and how these could have impact on the field, the company, or the department and their areas of interest and growth.

It's hard to give a bad talk that's structured this way.

author: alexolegimas
quoted_text:
Today I mourn the loss of a great person and economist.  Jim Andreoni has been a friend and mentor since the early 1990s.  Jim was a Wisconsin kid through and through. Big heart, always friendly and wise, and one of the most caring people you will ever meet.  

Professionally, Jim inspired us all across areas as diverse as charitable giving and GARP.  At one point I was introducing Jim for a keynote and I simply pulled out my most recent working paper and showed the first page of the references. It was all Andreoni references. There was no more to say.  We lost an intellectual giant today but more importantly we lost a great human being. 

Jim, we will miss you deeply my friend.

大家好，Magpie 今天有一个很重要的更新，就是 Magpie 中的 Claude Code Provider 的实现方式，从之前的使用 claude -p 改为了直接使用 Claude Code TUI。当然这是可配置的，你可以设置回以前的方案。

关于为何做这个改动，其实一开始我是不太情愿的，因为使用 Claude Code TUI 去做这个实现的话，会特别多额外的工作。收益不是很高，甚至 streaming 没法完美实现。但是最近发生了一件事情，让我觉得我不得不得不做这个改动了，就是有人发现直接使用 claude -p 在 5 小时窗口情况下，会比用 Claude Code TUI 多花两倍的 Token（虽然 Claude 今天已经取消了5小时窗口，但是我不确定 Anthropic 以后会不会有其他的区别对待）

换成直接用 TUI 方式实现，除了能够让我们的额度消耗跟直接使用 TUI 一模一样之外，另外一个更大的优势就是在 Magpie 使用 Claude Code Provider 跟用户直接使用 Claude Code TUI 是一模一样的，几乎没有了被检测出来在第三方使用导致封号的风险。

The left understands that power is a form of currency. So if you want it, you have to buy it, with some other form of currency. Such as money. 

The right thinks that political power is a side effect... something that you naturally accumulate while doing business.

Possibly this is because most wealthy right-wing people are investors. They start a project, or put money into it, and they expect to get their money back and then some. That's what they are used to.

America, look at Europe. That is your future if you vote blue on Tuesday.

Vote like your life depends on it. Because the life you know does. Your right to speak, to build, to raise your kids the way you choose, to keep what you earn. Europe had all of that too. Then one day we looked up and it was gone.

I'm French. I live in it. So let me show you what the Democratic Party's ideal society looks like, because it already exists. It's called the European Union.

In Europe, an unelected Commission in Brussels writes the rules for 450 million people. Nobody voted for Ursula von der Leyen. Nobody can vote her out.

In Europe, Brussels fined X €120 million under its new rulebook for online platforms. When Washington stood up for X, Brussels said it would fight.

In Europe, they keep trying to scan your private messages. The Parliament killed it. The bureaucracy brought it back. 314 elected representatives voted no, and it became law anyway.

In Europe, when Romanian voters picked the wrong candidate in 2024, the election was simply cancelled.

In Europe, if you post the wrong thing, the police can knock on your door at 6am. Ask the Germans.

In Europe, we destroyed our own industry in the name of climate and called it progress.

Now look at the Democratic Party. A "Disinformation Governance Board." Federal pressure on platforms to take down posts, which Zuckerberg himself admitted. Climate mandates. Borders treated as an inconvenience. Same playbook, same conferences, same worldview: ordinary people can't be trusted, experts and institutions should decide for them.

The Democratic Party is the EU with an American accent.

That's why Tuesday is not a normal midterm. It's a vote on American sovereignty. Either America stays a nation where the people decide, or it becomes one more province run by the same transnational class that is running Europe into the ground.

Europe didn't lose its freedom in a day. It lost it one regulation at a time, one "emergency" at a time, while everyone thought it was boring politics. You still have the choice. We barely do.

And while you're at it, name the root. Communism killed close to 100 million people in the 20th century. Treat it like the other totalitarian ideology of that century: no place in American government, no place in American classrooms except as a warning.

Vote red. Bring your family. Bring your friends.

Europe is watching. We're counting on you.

text:
Jane Street put 12 GB of its real trading data online with a $120K prize.

The f*cking trap hidden inside it explains why most traders go broke while being RIGHT.

The scoring rule was simple: predict nothing, score zero.

But if your model was right and too confident, you scored BELOW zero. Worse than doing nothing.

The math behind it is one line:

score = 2m - m²

m is how big you bet compared to the right size. At m = 1 you win the most. At m = 2 you win nothing. Past that you lose, even when you're right.

It's the same curve as the Kelly formula. LTCM had two Nobel winners, ran 25x leverage and lost $4.6B in four months.

Being wrong is not what kills traders. Being right at the wrong size is.

The full paper and the prompt that checks your sizing are in the replies.

text:
As far as I know, Mysten Labs is the only blockchain company that has consistently stayed one step ahead when it comes to security best practices.

A few examples of what our cryptographers and security researchers have pioneered:

- Native multisig without additional gas costs. We deliberately designed Sui to accommodate larger transaction sizes, making multisig a first-class security feature rather than an expensive add-on. Our cryptographers were among the first to productionize advanced multisignature techniques, even before Facebook’s Libra.

- Cryptographic agility and post-quantum readiness. From pioneering production-ready stateless post-quantum signatures to developing the first backward-compatible post-quantum solutions, our team has consistently pushed the boundaries. This includes enabling cryptographic upgrades and key rotation while preserving the same blockchain address (afaik the first crypto agility design in decentralized ledgers is attributed to my team).

- Modern hardware wallet security. We’ve recently taken additional steps to incentivize startups to build the next generation of secure hardware wallets. With what we see in the market, this is one way.

- AI-powered vulnerability detection. Sui was the first blockchain to introduce AI-driven bug detection through BugDar, back then presenting  at Google’s Next conference. We knew AI would mess up security.

- Recovering the seemingly unrecoverable. We created KelpMe, introducing innovative approaches to recovering assets after mnemonic loss or accidental transfers to incorrect addresses, problems traditionally considered practically impossible to solve. KelpMe also won the Bybit Hackathon, demonstrating the real-world potential of this innovation.

- Zero-knowledge authentication as a first-class primitive. We went far beyond using ZK for privacy or scaling. With innovations such as zkLogin and ZEE-CAT, and for a while the most used ZK app in the planet, we demonstrated how zero-knowledge cryptography could fundamentally transform authentication.

- Proofs of solvency and exchange accountability. Undeniably, we’re the leaders. Our cryptographers designed some of the most advanced proof-of-solvency protocols and identified critical weaknesses in approaches used by major exchanges and auditing firms.

- World-class academic research at startup speed. Mysten Labs has systematically pushed the boundaries of academic research productivity, achieving publication records that are extraordinary for a startup. Our researchers reached an incredible milestone of 5 papers accepted at ACM CCS and 4 at Financial Cryptography (FC) in the same year, two of the world’s most prestigious venues in cybersecurity and applied cryptography. And so many best paper awards.
- Binary transparency with Walrus sites and crypto guard. Reality is we should have pushed further making it the standard for any crypto website, but at the same time we indeed genuinely try to fix the internet.
- Scion from our Swiss team, IMO the future of internet communication, kill DoS, native packet protection.

That’s a phenomenal achievement even for established university research groups, let alone a startup simultaneously building and securing a major blockchain ecosystem.

And these are just a few examples.

When you consider the size of our team and the breadth of its contributions, even compared with the much larger Ethereum ecosystem, I genuinely believe Mysten Labs has been one of the most impactful organizations in blockchain cybersecurity, with innovations that are applied in the whole financial sector.

What makes this particularly remarkable is that we didn’t just publish research or build theoretical solutions. We repeatedly turned cutting-edge cryptographic research into production systems, often years ahead of broader industry adoption. No other org ever came close to that. Now with the AI vision of Evan, Mysten will do more miracles 🤞
